1.name: Calcium Chloride
1.description: Inorganic salt used as a firming agent, electrolyte source, and to control texture in foods.
1.benefits: Provides calcium nutrient, helps maintain food texture and firmness
1.risks: Irritation risk to skin and mucous membranes at high concentrations, ingestion toxicity low at typical food use levels

2.name: Magnesium Chloride
2.description: An inorganic salt used as a dietary supplement and in small amounts as a food additive. It contributes magnesium ions which are essential minerals for many physiological functions.
2.benefits: Provides bioavailable magnesium essential for muscle and nerve function, electrolyte balance, and enzymatic reactions
2.risks: Gastrointestinal irritation and laxative effects at high oral doses, irritation risk if in direct skin contact in concentrated form

3.name: Potassium Bicarbonate
3.description: Potassium bicarbonate is a potassium salt used as a leavening agent, pH buffer, and acidity regulator in food products.
3.benefits: Regulates acidity, acts as leavening agent, source of dietary potassium

4.name: Electrolytes
4.description: Minerals such as sodium, potassium, calcium, and magnesium that help maintain fluid balance and electric activity in the body.
4.benefits: Supports hydration, nerve function, muscle contraction, and electrolyte balance
4.risks: Excessive intake may cause electrolyte imbalance, hypertension, or kidney strain

5.name: Sodium Bicarbonate
5.description: An alkaline salt used as a mild abrasive, pH adjuster, and deodorizer in cleaning products. Generally recognized as safe and non-toxic at typical low use concentrations.
5.benefits: Effective mild abrasive, pH buffering agent, deodorizer, non-toxic, biodegradable
5.risks: Mild skin irritation possible in rare cases with high exposure

6.name: Magnesium Sulfate
6.description: An inorganic salt commonly used as a dietary supplement and laxative, also found in bath salts for topical use.
6.benefits: Provides magnesium essential for muscle and nerve function, electrolyte balance, mild laxative effect
6.risks: Irritation if ingested in high doses, potential laxative effects, possible skin dryness or irritation with topical use

8.name: Bromide
8.description: Bromide is a halide ion derived from bromine, commonly found in various industrial and chemical applications. It can be present as inorganic salts or as organic brominated compounds.
8.risks: Toxicity from ingestion or chronic exposure, potential neurotoxicity, interference with iodine uptake affecting thyroid function, possible contamination with brominated compounds

9.name: Chloride
9.description: An essential inorganic anion commonly found in body fluids and chloride-containing compounds. It helps maintain fluid balance and acid-base equilibrium.
9.benefits: Supports electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and proper nerve and muscle function
9.risks: Excessive intake may contribute to hypertension and cardiovascular risk when associated with high sodium intake

10.name: Sulfate
10.description: A chemical compound containing the sulfate ion (SO4²⁻), commonly used in personal care products as surfactants (e.g., sodium lauryl sulfate) due to their cleansing and foaming properties.
10.benefits: Effective cleansing and foaming agent in personal care products
10.risks: Skin irritation, eye irritation, potential to disrupt skin barrier with prolonged exposure

12.name: Total Trihalomethanes
12.description: Group of chemical compounds formed as disinfection byproducts during chlorination of water, including chloroform, bromodichloromethane, dibromochloromethane, and bromoform.
12.risks: Carcinogenic potential, contaminated drinking water, regulatory limits due to toxicity, ingestion toxicity

13.name: Sodium Sulfate
13.description: Inorganic salt used as a filler or bulking agent in cleaning products. Typically low toxicity and low irritancy under normal use conditions.

14.name: Gross Alpha
14.description: Measures the total alpha radiation emitted by all alpha-emitting radionuclides in a water sample, such as uranium and thorium, to assess overall alpha radiation levels.
14.risks: Internal tissue damage and increased cancer risk due to their ionizing nature when ingested or inhaled.

15.name: Gross Beta
15.description: Measures the total beta radiation emitted by all beta-emitting radionuclides in a water sample, such as strontium-90 and cesium-137, to evaluate overall beta radiation levels.
15.risks: Internal tissue damage, increased cancer risk, and potential harm to the thyroid.

16.name: Radium 226/228
16.description: Radioactive isotopes of radium that emit alpha, beta, and gamma radiation. Not used as a food ingredient. Exposure poses significant radiological health risks including cancer and radiation sickness.
16.risks: Radiation exposure, carcinogenicity, bone cancer, organ damage, radiation sickness

17.name: Silica
17.description: Inert mineral compound (silicon dioxide) used primarily as an anti-caking agent and absorbent in food and industrial products.
17.benefits: Prevents clumping and improves texture in powdered products
17.risks: Minor respiratory irritation risk from inhalation of fine dust; minimal concern at typical ingestion levels

20.name: Arsenic
20.description: A toxic metalloid element found in the environment often as a contaminant in water, soil, and food.
20.risks: Carcinogenicity, acute and chronic poisoning, neurotoxicity, skin lesions, cardiovascular disease, contamination risk

21.name: Barium
21.description: A soft, silvery alkaline earth metal used in various industrial applications and sometimes as a contrast agent in medical imaging.
21.risks: Toxic if ingested or inhaled, can cause muscle weakness, cardiovascular effects, and respiratory paralysis, contamination risk

22.name: Fluoride
22.description: Inorganic compound commonly used in dental care products to prevent tooth decay through enamel remineralization.
22.benefits: Prevents dental caries, strengthens tooth enamel
22.risks: Dental fluorosis with excessive ingestion, neurotoxicity concerns at high exposure, skeletal fluorosis in chronic high doses

23.name: Nitrate (as NO₃⁻)
23.description: An inorganic ion commonly found in soil, water, and food, used as a preservative and nutrient source in agriculture and food processing.
23.benefits: Used as a food preservative to inhibit microbial growth, supports plant nutrition and growth
23.risks: Potential to form nitrosamines which are carcinogenic, methemoglobinemia risk especially in infants, contamination from agricultural runoff

24.name: Uranium
24.description: A radioactive heavy metal element used primarily as fuel in nuclear reactors and in military applications.
24.benefits: None in food or cosmetic applications
24.risks: Radioactivity leading to radiation poisoning, heavy metal toxicity causing kidney damage, carcinogenic potential, environmental persistence

25.name: Dipotassium Phosphate
25.description: An inorganic salt used as a buffering agent, emulsifier, and nutrient source providing potassium and phosphate ions in food and beverages.
25.benefits: Provides potassium and phosphate electrolytes, stabilizes pH in formulations
25.risks: Excessive intake may contribute to mineral imbalance, potential renal burden in sensitive individuals

26.name: Bicarbonate Alkalinity (as HCO3)
26.description: Bicarbonate is a form of alkalinity commonly found in water and biological systems, acting as a buffer to maintain pH balance. In food and beverage contexts, it contributes to regulating acidity and can affect flavor and preservation. It is generally recognized as safe when consumed within typical dietary levels.
26.benefits: Buffers acid, supports pH balance, aids digestion, contributes to electrolyte balance
26.risks: Excessive intake may lead to alkalosis or digestive disturbances in sensitive individuals

29.name: Bromodichloromethane
29.description: Bromodichloromethane is a trihalomethane compound commonly found as a disinfection byproduct in chlorinated drinking water. It is not a food ingredient but a chemical contaminant associated with water treatment processes.
29.risks: Carcinogenic potential, liver and kidney toxicity, reproductive toxicity, neurotoxicity, possible endocrine disruption

30.name: Chloroform
30.description: A halogenated organic solvent formerly used as an anesthetic and industrial solvent. It is not a food ingredient and is toxic to humans with potential carcinogenic effects. Exposure is primarily hazardous via inhalation, ingestion, or skin contact.
30.risks: Toxicity, carcinogenicity, respiratory depression, liver and kidney damage, central nervous system depression

31.name: Dibromochloromethane
31.description: A halogenated methane disinfection byproduct commonly found in chlorinated drinking water. Listed as a potential human carcinogen by the EPA and associated with adverse health effects upon ingestion.
31.risks: Potential carcinogen, reproductive toxicity, liver and kidney damage, mutagenicity

32.name: Radon
32.description: Radon is a naturally occurring radioactive gas resulting from the decay of uranium in soil, rock, and water. It is not a food ingredient and is considered a hazardous material due to its radioactive properties. Exposure mainly occurs by inhalation of indoor air containing radon gas and is a known human carcinogen.
32.risks: Lung cancer, radioactive exposure, respiratory hazards

33.name: Potassium Chloride
33.description: Potassium chloride is an inorganic salt used as a calcium lactate stabilizer and a potassium source in food and pharmaceutical applications.
33.benefits: Provides essential potassium electrolyte, stabilizes calcium lactate to prevent precipitation or crystallization
33.risks: Excessive intake associated with hyperkalemia in sensitive populations, potential gastrointestinal irritation at high doses

34.name: Chloramine
34.description: Chloramine is a disinfectant used primarily to treat drinking water as an alternative to chlorine. It is formed by combining chlorine and ammonia and is used to control microbial growth. It is not a food ingredient for consumption but a water treatment chemical.
34.benefits: Effective water disinfectant, longer-lasting residual disinfectant in distribution systems compared to chlorine, reduces formation of some harmful chlorinated by-products
34.risks: Respiratory irritation, skin irritation, potential formation of harmful disinfection by-products, possible toxic effects at high levels

35.name: CO2
35.description: Carbon dioxide (CO2) is a naturally occurring, colorless, and odorless gas used in food and beverage processing for carbonation, preservation, and packaging. In the body, it is a normal metabolic byproduct expelled during respiration.
35.risks: None at concentrations typically used in food and beverages

38.name: Chromium (hexavalent)
38.description: Hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)) is a toxic form of chromium used industrially; it is a known carcinogen with no safe nutritional role. Not a food ingredient, but a hazardous material primarily encountered in occupational or environmental exposure.
38.risks: Carcinogenicity, respiratory sensitization, skin irritation, genotoxicity, occupational exposure hazards

39.name: Nitrite
39.description: Nitrites are food additives commonly used as preservatives and color fixatives in processed meats. They help prevent bacterial growth, especially Clostridium botulinum, but can form potentially carcinogenic nitrosamines under certain conditions.
39.benefits: Prevents growth of harmful bacteria in processed meats, extends shelf life, maintains meat color and flavor
39.risks: Potential formation of carcinogenic nitrosamines, possible association with increased cancer risk, may cause methemoglobinemia in infants at high exposure

40.name: Bromate
40.description: Bromate is an oxidizing agent commonly formed as a byproduct during ozonation of water and can also be present in some baking processes involving bromate salts.
40.risks: Carcinogenicity, genotoxicity, regulatory restriction, ingestion toxicity

41.name: Calcium
41.description: Essential mineral involved in bone formation, muscle function, nerve transmission, and vascular contraction.
41.benefits: Supports bone health, muscle contraction, nerve signaling
41.risks: Excessive intake may cause hypercalcemia, kidney stones

42.name: Magnesium
42.description: Essential mineral involved in numerous biochemical reactions, including energy production, muscle and nerve function, and bone development.
42.benefits: Supports muscle and nerve function, contributes to bone health, involved in enzymatic reactions
42.risks: Gastrointestinal upset at very high doses, risk of overdose primarily in individuals with impaired kidney function

43.name: Potassium
43.description: Essential dietary mineral important for maintaining cellular function, nerve transmission, and muscle contraction.
43.benefits: Supports electrolyte balance, helps regulate blood pressure, essential for nerve and muscle function
43.risks: Hyperkalemia risk at excessive intake or impaired kidney function, minor ingestion toxicity at high doses

45.name: Sodium
45.description: Sodium is an essential electrolyte involved in fluid balance, nerve transmission, and muscle function.
45.benefits: Essential electrolyte, supports nerve transmission, aids fluid balance
45.risks: Hypertension and cardiovascular risk with excessive intake

46.name: Manganese
46.description: Essential trace mineral involved in enzymatic reactions, bone formation, and metabolism.
46.benefits: Supports antioxidant enzyme function, bone development, and metabolism
46.risks: Neurotoxicity at high exposure levels, impaired motor function with excessive intake

47.name: Aluminum
47.description: Metallic element commonly used in cookware, packaging, and cosmetics, with potential for human exposure via ingestion, inhalation, or skin contact.
47.benefits: None at typical consumer exposure levels
47.risks: Neurological toxicity at high exposure, potential accumulation in body tissues, possible respiratory irritation upon inhalation, contamination risk

49.name: Bromoform
49.description: Bromoform is a trihalomethane compound often formed as a byproduct during water chlorination and disinfection processes. It is not used as a food ingredient. Bromoform is considered a hazardous material due to its potential toxicity and carcinogenicity upon exposure.
49.risks: Toxicity, carcinogenic potential, respiratory irritation, central nervous system effects, environmental pollutant

58.name: Nickel
58.description: A metallic element commonly used in alloys, plating, and industrial applications. Not a food ingredient. In materials context, exposure via skin contact or inhalation can cause allergic reactions and respiratory issues. Not suitable for ingestion.
58.risks: Allergic contact dermatitis, respiratory sensitization, carcinogenic potential upon inhalation, systemic toxicity if ingested in large amounts

59.name: Zinc
59.description: Essential trace mineral important for immune function, enzyme activity, and cellular metabolism.
59.benefits: Supports immune system, wound healing, enzyme function, and growth
59.risks: Excessive intake can cause gastrointestinal irritation, interfere with copper absorption, and cause toxicity

60.name: Chlorine Dioxide
60.description: Chlorine dioxide is a strong oxidizing agent used as a disinfectant and bleaching agent. It is a gaseous or dissolved compound used in cleaning formulations at low concentrations.
60.benefits: Effective broad-spectrum disinfectant and sanitizer, effective against bacteria, viruses, and spores
60.risks: Respiratory irritation, eye irritation, skin irritation, toxicity at higher inhalation exposures, potential oxidative damage

61.name: Chlorine
61.description: Chlorine is a highly reactive halogen gas widely used as a disinfectant and bleaching agent in cleaning products. It is typically present as a gas or in aqueous solutions such as hypochlorite. Known for strong oxidizing properties.
61.benefits: Effective broad-spectrum disinfectant and bleaching agent, rapid antimicrobial activity
61.risks: Respiratory irritation, skin irritation, eye irritation, corrosive effects, toxic by inhalation, potential for release of toxic chlorine gas

62.name: Lead
62.description: Heavy metal element with no biological function, toxic to multiple organ systems.
62.risks: Neurotoxicity, developmental toxicity, cardiovascular damage, kidney damage, carcinogenicity, contamination risk

64.name: Cadmium
64.description: Cadmium is a heavy metal element that occurs naturally but can accumulate via industrial pollution. It is toxic to humans with no biological function.
64.risks: Heavy metal toxicity, kidney damage, bone demineralization, carcinogenicity, regulatory bans in consumer products

65.name: Copper
65.description: Copper is a trace essential mineral necessary for various enzymatic processes, iron metabolism, and neurological function. It is required in small amounts in diet but is toxic at high doses. In non-food contexts, copper metal or compounds can cause skin irritation or toxicity if improperly handled.
65.benefits: Essential trace mineral, supports enzymatic functions, iron metabolism, connective tissue formation, and neurological health
65.risks: Toxicity in excess, gastrointestinal distress if ingested in large amounts, skin irritation with direct prolonged contact or occupational exposure

66.name: Spring water
66.description: Water sourced from natural springs, typically free of contaminants and used for hydration or product formulation.

69.name: PFAS
69.description: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are synthetic fluorinated chemicals used for their water-, oil-, and stain-resistant properties in various consumer products and industrial applications.
69.risks: Persistence, bioaccumulation, potential carcinogenicity, endocrine disruption, immune system effects, contamination of water and soil

70.name: Tap water
70.description: Water supplied through municipal systems that is treated to meet safety standards for human consumption. Quality varies regionally and may contain trace minerals and disinfectant byproducts.
70.benefits: Essential for hydration, universal solvent, supports physiological functions, generally safe to drink in regulated areas
70.risks: Potential contaminants depending on local water quality, disinfectant byproducts, heavy metals in some areas

75.name: Mineral Water
75.description: Natural water containing various minerals such as calcium, magnesium, and bicarbonates; safe for consumption and often provides hydration along with trace mineral benefits. Regulated by FDA as a water source with specified mineral content.
75.benefits: Hydration, provides essential minerals like calcium and magnesium, may support bone health and electrolyte balance
75.risks: Potential contaminants if source is polluted, possible high sodium content in some mineral waters

76.name: Carbon Dioxide (CO2)
76.description: Carbon dioxide used as a food additive to carbonate beverages, creating effervescence and bubbly texture.
76.benefits: Provides carbonation and texture to beverages

77.name: Boron
77.description: Boron is a trace mineral found naturally in foods and water. It plays a role in bone health, hormone regulation, and cognitive function. While beneficial in small dietary amounts, excessive intake can be toxic.
77.benefits: Supports bone health, hormone regulation, cognitive function, anti-inflammatory effects
77.risks: Toxicity in high doses, nausea, hormonal imbalance

78.name: Thallium
78.description: A heavy metal element that is highly toxic to humans. It has no role as a food ingredient and is not approved for consumption. Exposure can occur through contaminated water, air, or industrial sources.
78.risks: Highly toxic, carcinogenic potential, neurotoxicity, organ damage, fatal poisoning

80.name: Antimony
80.description: A metalloid element not used as a food ingredient; primarily encountered as an environmental contaminant or in industrial contexts. Exposure can occur via inhalation, ingestion, or skin contact, often from mining, smelting, or manufacturing processes.
80.risks: Toxicity, respiratory irritation, skin irritation, potential carcinogenicity, chronic exposure can cause lung and heart problems

81.name: Beryllium
81.description: A toxic metal element not used as a food ingredient. Exposure primarily occurs via inhalation in industrial settings, causing serious respiratory diseases including chronic beryllium disease (berylliosis). It is not safe for ingestion or contact and has no nutritional value.
81.risks: Toxicity, chronic beryllium disease, lung cancer, respiratory sensitization, carcinogenicity

82.name: Iron
82.description: Essential mineral involved in oxygen transport, energy metabolism, and various enzymatic processes in the body.
82.benefits: Supports oxygen transport via hemoglobin, essential for energy production, supports immune function
82.risks: Excessive intake can cause gastrointestinal irritation, iron overload leading to tissue damage, and interference with absorption of other minerals

83.name: Selenium
83.description: Essential trace mineral important for antioxidant defense and thyroid hormone metabolism.
83.benefits: Supports antioxidant enzymes, thyroid function, immune system support
83.risks: Toxicity at high doses leading to selenosis, gastrointestinal symptoms, hair loss, nail brittleness

84.name: Silver
84.description: Metallic element sometimes found as trace contamination in water and consumer products.
84.risks: Potential argyria with chronic ingestion at high levels, possible cellular toxicity in high doses

88.name: Carbon tetrachloride
88.description: Carbonate refers to salts or esters of carbonic acid containing the carbonate ion (CO3). In trace amounts (<1 mg), it typically appears as a minor component or impurity in various products.

104.name: Molybdenum
104.description: An essential trace mineral required for enzyme function, including metabolism of sulfur-containing amino acids and nitrogen fixation. Recognized as safe and necessary in small amounts for human nutrition.
104.benefits: Essential cofactor for enzymes, supports metabolic processes, antioxidant functions
104.risks: Excessive intake may cause gout-like symptoms, joint pain, elevated uric acid levels

105.name: Added Sugar
105.description: Sugars incorporated into foods during processing or preparation, not naturally occurring in foods.
105.risks: Excessive intake associated with weight gain, dental caries, metabolic disturbances

107.name: Bisphenols
107.description: Bisphenols, including Bisphenol A (BPA) and related analogs, are industrial chemicals used in manufacturing plastics and resins. They are not food ingredients but materials that can contaminate food via packaging. They are endocrine disruptors with documented hormonal effects.
107.risks: Endocrine disruption, reproductive toxicity, developmental effects, potential carcinogenicity, metabolic disorders

110.name: Chlorodibromoacetic acid
110.description: A disinfection byproduct formed in chlorinated water; not used as a food ingredient. It is known to be a toxic environmental contaminant with potential carcinogenic and genotoxic effects.
110.risks: Carcinogenic potential, genotoxicity, environmental toxin, potential reproductive toxicity

112.name: Vanadium
112.description: Vanadium is a trace metal element found in various environmental sources and used in some industrial applications. It can enter the human body primarily through ingestion or inhalation.
112.benefits: None at typical consumer exposure levels
112.risks: Inhalation toxicity, potential heavy metal contamination, toxicity at high doses, respiratory and renal effects with exposure

118.name: Sunflower Oil
118.description: Edible oil extracted from sunflower seeds, predominantly composed of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA), mainly linoleic acid.
118.benefits: Source of unsaturated fats, vitamin E content, supports skin barrier and cardiovascular health when consumed in moderation
118.risks: High omega-6 fatty acid content, oxidative instability at high heat or long storage, excessive intake associated with weight gain

119.name: Canola Oil
119.description: Edible oil extracted from the seeds of the canola plant, primarily used as a cooking or salad oil with a fatty acid profile rich in monounsaturated fats and some polyunsaturated fats.
119.benefits: Source of monounsaturated fats, commonly used in food preparation
119.risks: PUFA-dominant oil, oxidation instability, potential mild irritant in topical use

125.name: Soluble Corn Fiber
125.description: A type of dietary fiber derived from corn starch, used to increase fiber content and reduce calories in food products.
125.benefits: Dietary fiber source, may improve bowel regularity and reduce caloric content in foods
125.risks: Excessive intake may cause gastrointestinal discomfort such as bloating or gas

138.name: Organic Jerusalem artichoke powder
138.description: Powdered form of Jerusalem artichoke, a tuber rich in dietary fiber, particularly inulin, a prebiotic fructan that supports gut health. Organic designation indicates cultivation without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. Generally recognized as safe for consumption with noted digestive benefits.
138.benefits: Prebiotic dietary fiber (inulin), supports gut microbiota, may improve digestion, low glycemic index, potential blood sugar regulation
138.risks: Digestive discomfort such as bloating or gas in sensitive individuals or when consumed in large amounts

141.name: Pea protein
141.description: Protein isolate derived from Pisum sativum (pea), used primarily as a plant-based protein source in food products.
141.benefits: Rich source of plant protein, supports muscle maintenance, alternative for dairy and soy allergies
141.risks: Possible allergenicity in sensitive individuals, processing may involve anti-nutritional factors if not treated

145.name: Polydextrose
145.description: Polydextrose is a synthetic polymer of glucose used primarily as a humectant, bulking agent, and soluble fiber in food products.
145.benefits: Low-calorie bulking agent, source of soluble fiber, supports digestive health
145.risks: Digestive discomfort at high intake, potential laxative effect

149.name: Stevia Sweetener
149.description: Natural non-nutritive sweetener derived from the leaves of the Stevia rebaudiana plant, primarily composed of steviol glycosides.
149.benefits: Non-caloric sweetener, does not raise blood glucose levels, useful for sugar reduction
149.risks: Possible mild gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals, rare allergic reactions

151.name: Acesulfame Potassium
151.description: Acesulfame Potassium (Ace-K) is a synthetic, calorie-free sweetener used to provide sweetness in food and beverages without added calories.
151.benefits: Calorie-free sweetener, helps reduce sugar intake, stable under heat and acidic conditions
151.risks: Potential gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses, possible concerns over chronic toxicity though regulatory bodies consider it safe at typical use levels

153.name: Strontium-90
153.description: A radioactive isotope produced by nuclear fission found in nuclear fallout. It is not a food ingredient and poses significant health hazards when ingested, inhaled, or contacted, due to its beta radiation emissions and propensity to accumulate in bones.
153.risks: Radioactive contamination, bone cancer, leukemia, radiation sickness, genetic damage, mutagenesis

155.name: Turbidity
155.description: Turbidity is a measure of the level of particles such as sediment, plankton, or organic by-products, in a body of water.
155.benefits: It can indicate the presence of pathogenic microorganisms.

157.name: Borate
157.description: Borates are boron-containing compounds commonly used in industrial applications, detergents, cosmetics, and as preservatives. They are not used as food ingredients and have potential toxicity concerns upon ingestion or significant exposure. Borates exhibit mild antiseptic and antifungal properties but pose health risks mainly due to their potential toxicity when absorbed or ingested.
157.benefits: Antiseptic, antifungal properties in non-food uses
157.risks: Toxicity, reproductive toxicity, developmental toxicity, skin irritation, inhalation hazards

162.name: Radium 228
162.description: Radium-228 is a radioactive isotope of radium, a naturally occurring radioactive element in the actinide series, known for its alpha and beta radiation emissions.
162.risks: Radioactivity, carcinogenic potential, radiation poisoning risk, contamination hazard

163.name: Radium 226
163.description: Radium-226 is a radioactive isotope of radium, historically used in luminous paints and medical treatments. It emits alpha, beta, and gamma radiation.
163.risks: Radioactive contamination, high radiotoxicity, carcinogenicity, bone deposition leading to bone cancer, radiation sickness

166.name: Chromium (Total)
166.description: Chromium is a trace mineral required in small amounts for normal carbohydrate, lipid, and protein metabolism, often included as a nutrient supplement. Total chromium measures all forms including trivalent (Cr3+) and hexavalent (Cr6+) chromium.
166.benefits: Supports normal glucose metabolism and insulin function at essential trace levels
166.risks: Potential toxicity from hexavalent chromium (Cr6+) forms, occupational inhalation toxicity, contamination risk if Cr6+ present, ingestion toxicity possible only with contaminated forms

172.name: Sunflower Lecithin
172.description: A natural phospholipid extracted from sunflower seeds, used primarily as an emulsifier in food products to improve texture and shelf life.
172.benefits: Emulsifier, improves food texture and stability, soy-free alternative to soy lecithin
172.risks: Sensitization potential in sensitive individuals, minimal ingestion toxicity at typical use levels

192.name: Total Dissolved Solids (TDS)
192.description: A measure of combined inorganic and organic substances dissolved in water, including minerals, salts, metals, and organic matter. It is not a food ingredient but an indicator of water quality and composition.
192.benefits: Indicator of mineral content in water, can reflect water purity and nutritional mineral levels
192.risks: Depends on the nature of dissolved solids, potential for heavy metals or contaminants if high

194.name: Endosulfan Sulfate
194.description: Inorganic anion commonly found in water and various food sources; typically present as sulfate salts or dissolved ions.
194.benefits: None specific at typical dietary levels

226.name: Sodium Citrates
226.description: Sodium salts of citric acid used as acidity regulators and emulsifying salts in foods and pharmaceuticals.
226.benefits: Acidity regulation, buffering capacity, emulsification support

229.name: Whey Protein Concentrate
229.description: A dairy-derived protein source obtained from the liquid remaining after milk has been curdled and strained. It provides a mixture of proteins, lactose, and minerals.
229.benefits: High-quality protein source, supports muscle protein synthesis and recovery
229.risks: Allergic reactions in individuals with milk allergy, potential lactose intolerance symptoms in sensitive individuals

243.name: Pyridoxine Hydrochloride
243.description: A synthetic form of vitamin B6 used as a dietary supplement and food additive to support normal metabolism and neurological function.
243.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, neurological function, and red blood cell production
243.risks: High-dose supplementation may cause sensory neuropathy in rare cases, minor irritation if used topically

255.name: Phthalates
255.description: Phthalates are a group of synthetic chemicals used as plasticizers to increase flexibility in plastics and found as contaminants in various consumer products including personal care items.
255.risks: Endocrine disruption, reproductive toxicity, developmental toxicity, potential carcinogenicity, contamination in consumer products

267.name: Organic Lime Juice
267.description: Organic lime juice is derived from organically grown limes and is rich in vitamin C, antioxidants, and minor phytonutrients. In the diet, it can provide immune support and aid in iron absorption. In food products, it acts as a natural acidulant and flavor enhancer.
267.benefits: Source of vitamin C, antioxidant properties, supports iron absorption, natural flavoring
267.risks: Mild dental enamel erosion with excessive consumption

268.name: Organic Orange Juice
268.description: Juice extracted from oranges grown without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. Contains vitamin C, sugars, and flavonoids.
268.benefits: Source of vitamin C, antioxidants, and hydration
268.risks: High natural sugar content, potential dental erosion with excessive consumption

313.name: Polytetrafluoroethylene / PTFE
313.description: A synthetic fluoropolymer widely used for non-stick coatings in cookware and various industrial applications. Stable under normal conditions but can release toxic fumes when overheated above 260°C (500°F). Not a food ingredient, classified as a material with inhalation risks in thermal degradation.
313.benefits: Durable, chemically inert, non-stick surface for cookware, low friction
313.risks: Toxic fumes on overheating (polymer fume fever), respiratory irritation, environmental persistence

327.name: Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP)
327.description: A synthetic plasticizer used to increase the flexibility of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) products. Not intended for food consumption; known for potential endocrine-disrupting effects and used in some materials including medical devices and plastics.
327.benefits: Used industrially to increase plastic flexibility, no health benefits for consumption
327.risks: Endocrine disruption, reproductive toxicity, potential carcinogenicity, developmental toxicity

352.name: Phenols
352.description: A class of aromatic organic compounds characterized by one or more hydroxyl groups attached to an aromatic ring, found naturally in plants and used in various industrial and pharmaceutical applications.
352.benefits: Antioxidant properties, antimicrobial activity, natural preservative effect
352.risks: Skin and respiratory irritation, potential sensitization, toxic if ingested in high amounts, potential contamination with harmful derivatives depending on source and purity

365.name: 4-Isopropyltoluene / p-CYMENE
365.description: p-Cymene is a naturally occurring aromatic organic compound found in various essential oils such as cumin and thyme oils. It is used in fragrances, flavorings, and as an intermediate in chemical syntheses. In food, it occurs as a minor component and is generally recognized as safe in low concentrations. However, inhalation or high exposure can cause respiratory irritation and potential neurotoxicity in animal studies.
365.benefits: Naturally occurring flavor and fragrance component, antimicrobial properties in essential oils
365.risks: Respiratory irritation, potential neurotoxicity at high exposure, skin irritation in sensitive individuals

372.name: Chloromethane
372.description: Chloromethane (methyl chloride) is a volatile organic compound used industrially as a solvent and refrigerant. It is not approved as a food ingredient and is considered toxic with potential harmful effects if ingested, inhaled, or absorbed. It poses health risks from exposure and is not safe for consumption.
372.risks: Toxicity, central nervous system depression, respiratory issues, carcinogenic potential, neurotoxicity

380.name: m-Xylene
380.description: m-Xylene is an aromatic hydrocarbon used primarily as an industrial solvent and in chemical manufacturing. It is not a food ingredient and is considered a hazardous material due to its toxicity and potential health risks upon inhalation, ingestion, or skin contact.
380.risks: Neurotoxicity, respiratory tract irritation, central nervous system depression, carcinogenic potential, skin irritation, environmental toxicity

385.name: Naphthalene
385.description: A polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon used in mothballs as a fumigant and insect repellent. Known to be toxic and potentially carcinogenic with prolonged exposure.
385.risks: Inhalation toxicity, hemolytic anemia, skin irritation, respiratory irritation, carcinogenicity, neurotoxicity

386.name: o-Xylene
386.description: o-Xylene is an aromatic hydrocarbon commonly used as a solvent in industrial applications. It is not a food ingredient and is considered a chemical material with potential toxic effects upon inhalation, ingestion, or skin contact.
386.risks: Neurotoxicity, respiratory irritation, skin irritation, central nervous system effects, potential carcinogenicity with chronic exposure

398.name: Chlorodibromomethane
398.description: Chlorodibromomethane is a halogenated methane compound often found as a disinfection byproduct in chlorinated water. It is not used as a food ingredient and is considered an environmental contaminant with potential toxic effects.
398.risks: Potential carcinogenicity, reproductive toxicity, environmental contaminant, water disinfection byproduct toxicity

399.name: Ammonia
399.description: Inorganic alkaline compound commonly used as a cleaning agent and degreaser. Known for strong alkalinity and volatility.
399.benefits: Effective cleaning and degreasing agent, removes stains and cuts grease
399.risks: Eye irritation, respiratory irritation, skin irritation, potential for respiratory sensitization, hazardous if inhaled at high concentrations

402.name: Iodine
402.description: Essential trace element necessary for thyroid hormone synthesis and normal thyroid function.
402.benefits: Supports thyroid hormone production, essential for metabolic regulation and normal growth
402.risks: Excessive intake may cause thyroid dysfunction or iodine poisoning, possible allergic reactions at high doses

408.name: Cobalt
408.description: A naturally occurring metal element used industrially and as a dietary trace mineral. While cobalt is essential in small amounts as a component of vitamin B12, excessive exposure, particularly by inhalation or skin contact in industrial settings, can pose health risks including respiratory and skin sensitization, and potential carcinogenicity. Cobalt metal is not a food ingredient and poses toxicity risks when used inappropriately.
408.benefits: Essential trace element as part of vitamin B12 (in biological form), important for red blood cell formation
408.risks: Respiratory sensitization, skin sensitization, carcinogenic potential, toxicity with inhalation or ingestion in excess, systemic toxicity

410.name: Lithium
410.description: A naturally occurring alkali metal and trace element found in rocks, soil, and water. Used therapeutically as lithium carbonate for bipolar disorder and as an OTC supplement (lithium orotate, lithium aspartate) for mood support and neuroprotection. Has a narrow therapeutic index; serum levels above 1.5 mEq/L are toxic.
410.benefits: Mood stabilization and prevention of manic/depressive episodes at therapeutic doses; neuroprotective effects including potential protection against Alzheimer's disease; may support cognitive function at low doses; preliminary evidence for aiding alcohol cessation
410.risks: Toxicity at high doses (serum >1.5 mEq/L); nephrotoxicity with long-term use; thyroid dysfunction (hypothyroidism, goiter); neurological side effects (tremor, cognitive impairment, ataxia); cardiac arrhythmias; teratogenic risk; narrow therapeutic window; OTC supplements are unregulated and lack FDA approval for any condition

418.name: Microplastics
418.description: Small plastic particles less than 5mm in size originating from plastic debris breakdown or manufactured as microbeads.
418.risks: Environmental persistence, contamination of food and water, potential ingestion toxicity, bioaccumulation, potential endocrine disruption

455.name: Carbon Disulfide
455.description: A volatile, colorless liquid used industrially as a solvent and in the manufacture of viscose rayon and cellophane. Not a food ingredient; exposure concerns arise from inhalation and skin contact in occupational settings.
455.risks: Neurotoxicity, reproductive toxicity, cardiovascular toxicity, respiratory irritation, chronic exposure risks, carcinogenic potential

485.name: Sodium Fluoride
485.description: Inorganic compound used primarily as a fluoridating agent in dental care products to prevent dental caries by enhancing tooth enamel resistance.
485.benefits: Dental caries prevention through enamel remineralization
485.risks: Ingestion toxicity at high doses including acute poisoning, potential skeletal fluorosis with chronic excessive exposure, irritation risk in concentrated topical use

513.name: Natural flavors
513.description: Complex mixtures of flavor compounds derived from natural sources, often processed with solvents and additives.
513.benefits: Enhance flavor profile without added nutrients
513.risks: Lack of transparency in composition, potential presence of solvent residues, possible allergens, ultra-processed nature

516.name: Mango puree
516.description: Pureed form of mango fruit providing natural flavor and texture to food products.
516.benefits: Source of dietary fiber, vitamins (especially vitamin C and A precursors), natural flavor

517.name: Orange juice
517.description: Fruit juice derived from oranges, typically containing natural sugars, vitamin C, and other nutrients. Used in food products for flavor and nutrient contribution.
517.benefits: Source of vitamin C and antioxidants, provides flavor and hydration
517.risks: High natural sugar content, potential dental erosion with frequent consumption, possible allergenic reactions in sensitive individuals

518.name: Citric acid
518.description: A weak organic acid commonly used as a preservative and acidulant in food and cosmetic products.
518.benefits: Preservative properties, pH adjuster, flavor enhancer, chelating agent to improve product stability
518.risks: Irritation to skin and eyes at high concentrations, potential for mild sensitization with prolonged exposure

519.name: Hibiscus
519.description: Botanical ingredient derived from Hibiscus flowers, commonly used in beverages and topical products for color and flavor.
519.benefits: Flavoring agent, natural colorant, contains antioxidants
519.risks: Possible allergic reactions or skin irritation in sensitive individuals

520.name: Raspberry puree
520.description: Raspberry puree is a food ingredient made from crushed raspberries, commonly used for flavor and color in foods and beverages. Water is often added to adjust consistency or concentration.
520.benefits: Source of natural flavor, contains dietary fiber and antioxidants

521.name: Raspberry juice
521.description: Juice extracted from raspberries, used primarily as a flavoring or colorant in food and beverage products.
521.benefits: Provides natural flavor and color, contains antioxidants such as vitamin C and polyphenols

522.name: Lime juice
522.description: Lime refers to the citrus fruit Citrus aurantiifolia or Citrus latifolia, used for its juice and flavor. It is a natural source of vitamin C and citric acid.
522.benefits: Provides vitamin C, antioxidant capacity, flavoring agent
522.risks: Irritant potential on skin or mucosa, phototoxicity risk especially with lime oil, ingestion generally safe at dietary levels

523.name: Natural essence
523.description: Concentrated extracts derived from natural sources such as plants, used primarily for flavoring or fragrance purposes.
523.benefits: Provides natural flavor or fragrance, can enhance sensory properties
523.risks: Potential allergen or sensitizer, variability in composition, possible contamination with solvents or impurities

524.name: Organic cane sugar
524.description: Sucrose extracted from sugarcane, used as a sweetener in foods and beverages.
524.risks: Excessive intake associated with dental caries, weight gain, elevated blood glucose

525.name: Organic agave inulin
525.description: Inulin is a fructan-type soluble dietary fiber extracted from organic agave plant. It functions as a prebiotic fiber that resists digestion and promotes beneficial gut bacteria growth.
525.benefits: Prebiotic fiber, supports gut microbiota, may improve bowel regularity
525.risks: Digestive discomfort at high doses such as bloating, gas, flatulence

527.name: Organic apple cider vinegar
527.description: Fermented apple juice primarily composed of acetic acid and water, commonly used as a flavoring agent and preservative.
527.benefits: Acetic acid content may support antimicrobial effects and flavor enhancement
527.risks: Irritation risk at high concentrations when applied to skin or mucous membranes, possible enamel erosion with excessive ingestion

528.name: Stevia
528.description: Natural non-nutritive sweetener derived from Stevia rebaudiana, used to provide sweetness without calories.
528.benefits: Calorie-free sweetening, low glycemic impact, suitable for diabetic and weight management diets
528.risks: Possible mild gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals, potential for rare allergic reactions

531.name: Phosphorus
531.description: Essential mineral involved in bone formation, energy metabolism, and cellular function.
531.benefits: Supports bone and teeth health, energy production, and cellular signaling
531.risks: Excessive intake may disrupt mineral balance and affect kidney function in vulnerable populations

542.name: Strontium
542.description: Strontium is an alkaline earth metal element found naturally in small amounts in the environment and in some minerals. In dietary supplements, strontium salts (e.g., strontium ranelate) have been used for bone health, but elemental strontium itself is not a nutrient.
542.benefits: May support bone density when used as specific salts under medical supervision
542.risks: Potential toxicity with excessive ingestion, possible interference with calcium metabolism, contamination risk from radioactive isotopes in certain contexts

543.name: Malic Acid
543.description: A naturally occurring organic acid primarily used as an acidity regulator and flavor enhancer in foods.
543.risks: Mild oral or dermal irritation at high concentrations

545.name: Potassium Benzoate
545.description: Potassium benzoate is a potassium salt of benzoic acid used as a preservative to inhibit the growth of mold, yeast, and some bacteria in acidic foods and beverages.
545.benefits: Prevents microbial spoilage, extends shelf life of acidic foods and beverages
545.risks: Irritation at high concentrations, potential formation of benzene under certain conditions, sensitization in rare cases

546.name: Sucralose
546.description: Sucralose is a non-nutritive artificial sweetener used to provide sweetness without calories.
546.benefits: Calorie-free sweetness, useful for sugar replacement, supports reduced caloric intake
546.risks: Possible gut microbiota alterations, potential digestive discomfort at high doses, heat instability leading to breakdown products

547.name: Green Tea Extract
547.description: Concentrated extract from green tea leaves containing polyphenols, primarily catechins like epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG). Commonly used as an antioxidant and for flavor.
547.benefits: Antioxidant properties, may support skin health and reduce oxidative stress
547.risks: Potential liver toxicity in high doses, possible interference with some medications, mild gastrointestinal irritation

548.name: Cherry Juice Concentrate
548.description: Concentrated juice derived from cherries, primarily composed of sugars, organic acids, and phytochemicals such as anthocyanins.
548.benefits: Source of antioxidants, phytochemicals like anthocyanins
548.risks: High sugar content, potential for dental caries with excessive consumption

549.name: Retinol
549.description: Retinol is a form of vitamin A, a fat-soluble vitamin essential for vision, immune function, and skin health. It is not part of the vitamin B complex. Retinol is recognized by the FDA as a vitamin with established dietary reference intakes.
549.benefits: Supports vision, immune function, cellular growth, skin health, antioxidant activity
549.risks: Hypervitaminosis A, liver toxicity at high intakes, teratogenic effects during pregnancy

550.name: Niacinamide
550.description: A form of vitamin B3 used primarily in foods and cosmetics for skin barrier support and metabolic functions.
550.benefits: Supports skin barrier integrity, improves skin appearance, essential nutrient
550.risks: Possible mild skin irritation or sensitization at high concentrations, none at typical use

551.name: Calcium Pantothenate
551.description: Calcium pantothenate is a stable, calcium salt form of pantothenic acid (vitamin B5), a water-soluble vitamin essential for coenzyme A synthesis and energy metabolism.
551.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, necessary for synthesis of coenzyme A, involved in fatty acid and carbohydrate metabolism
551.risks: Rare mild gastrointestinal upset at high doses

553.name: Biotin
553.description: Water-soluble B-vitamin (vitamin B7) essential for carboxylase enzyme function in fatty acid synthesis, gluconeogenesis, and amino acid metabolism.
553.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, coenzyme for key metabolic pathways
553.risks: Rare allergic reactions, possible interference with certain laboratory test results

554.name: Cyanocobalamin
554.description: Synthetic form of vitamin B12 used as a dietary supplement and food fortificant to prevent or treat B12 deficiency.
554.benefits: Prevents and treats vitamin B12 deficiency, supports red blood cell formation and neurological function
554.risks: Rare allergic reactions, potential cyanide exposure in very high doses, generally safe at recommended levels

557.name: Magnesium Malate
557.description: Magnesium malate is a compound of magnesium and malic acid, often used as a dietary supplement to provide bioavailable magnesium.
557.benefits: Source of magnesium, supports muscle and nerve function, involved in energy production
557.risks: Gastrointestinal upset at high doses, laxative effect

558.name: Cane sugar
558.description: Sucrose derived from sugarcane, used as a sweetener and flavor enhancer in food products.
558.benefits: Provides sweetness, energy source through carbohydrates
558.risks: Excessive intake associated with risk of obesity, dental caries, and metabolic disorders

559.name: Dextrose
559.description: A simple sugar (glucose) commonly used as a sweetener and energy source in food products.
559.benefits: Quick energy source, commonly used for sweetness and fermentation support
559.risks: Excessive intake may contribute to increased blood sugar levels and caloric intake

560.name: Potassium citrate
560.description: Potassium citrate is a potassium salt of citric acid used as a mineral supplement and alkalinizing agent to maintain electrolyte balance and urinary pH.
560.benefits: Electrolyte replenishment, urinary alkalinizer to reduce kidney stone risk, supports cellular and nerve function
560.risks: Hyperkalemia risk in patients with impaired renal function or excessive intake, gastrointestinal irritation at high doses

561.name: Sodium citrate
561.description: Sodium citrate is the trisodium salt of citric acid, used as a water softener and pH buffer in cleaning products. It is classified as an organic salt chelating agent derived from citrus acids.
561.benefits: Water softening, pH buffering, biodegradable, low toxicity
561.risks: Mild skin irritation at very high concentrations, eye irritation if directly contacted

562.name: Silicon dioxide
562.description: An anti-caking agent commonly used in food and pharmaceuticals to prevent clumping and improve texture.
562.benefits: Prevents clumping, improves flow properties in powders and granules
562.risks: Inhalation of fine particles may cause mild respiratory irritation; minimal risk at typical ingestion levels

566.name: Organic flavors
566.description: Flavoring agents derived from organic sources, though still subject to extraction and processing methods that may involve solvents or additives. 'Organic' label indicates source material but does not guarantee absence of processing chemicals.
566.benefits: Derived from organic sources, perceived as cleaner by consumers compared to conventional flavors
566.risks: May contain solvent residues, ultra-processed, lack of transparency, no significant nutritional value

567.name: Erythritol
567.description: A sugar alcohol used as a low-calorie sweetener, commonly used to replace sugar.
567.benefits: Low-calorie sweetener, does not raise blood glucose or insulin levels

568.name: Coconut water concentrate
568.description: Concentrated form of coconut water composed mainly of water, electrolytes, and natural sugars, used for flavor and hydration.

569.name: Acacia gum
569.description: A natural polysaccharide gum obtained from the sap of Acacia trees, used as a glazing agent to provide a protective coating and improve texture in food products.
569.benefits: Edible fiber source, stabilizer, emulsifier, improves texture and shelf-life of food products
569.risks: Possible allergen in sensitive individuals, potential minor gastrointestinal effects at high doses

570.name: Sea salt
570.description: Mineral substance primarily composed of sodium chloride, obtained through evaporation of seawater.
570.benefits: Essential electrolyte, supports nerve transmission, aids fluid balance
570.risks: Hypertension and cardiovascular risk with excessive intake

572.name: Green coffee bean extract
572.description: Extract derived from unroasted coffee beans containing chlorogenic acids and other polyphenols.
572.benefits: Antioxidant properties, potential mild modulation of glucose metabolism
572.risks: Irritation at high doses, potential mild gastrointestinal upset, caffeine-related effects

574.name: D-alpha tocopheryl acetate (Vitamin E)
574.description: Synthetic form of vitamin E (alpha-tocopherol) esterified with acetic acid to enhance stability. Used as an antioxidant and nutrient supplement in food and skincare products.
574.benefits: Antioxidant protecting lipids from oxidation, skin conditioning agent, vitamin E source
574.risks: Low irritation potential, rare allergic sensitization, minimal toxicity at typical use levels

575.name: Agave nectar
575.description: Sweetener derived from the agave plant, primarily composed of fructose and glucose sugars.
575.benefits: Sweetening agent, sweeter than sucrose requiring smaller quantities
575.risks: High fructose content associated with excessive caloric intake, potential contribution to weight gain and metabolic disturbances if consumed in excess

576.name: Cassava root fiber
576.description: Dietary fiber derived from the root of the cassava plant (Manihot esculenta), used primarily as a source of insoluble fiber in food products.
576.benefits: Source of insoluble dietary fiber, supports digestive regularity, gluten-free fiber alternative
576.risks: Potential cyanogenic glycoside contamination if improperly processed, mild digestive intolerance in sensitive individuals

581.name: Calendula flower extract
581.description: Calendula flower extract is derived from the petals of Calendula officinalis and is commonly used for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties in both food and topical products.
581.benefits: Anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, promotes wound healing, antimicrobial effects
581.risks: Rare allergic reactions, potential interaction with sedative medications

583.name: Ginger juice
583.description: Juice extracted from the rhizome of the ginger plant (Zingiber officinale), commonly used as a flavoring agent and in beverages.
583.benefits: Flavor enhancement, natural antioxidant compounds, traditional digestive aid
583.risks: Mild skin and mucous membrane irritation possible in sensitive individuals, potential allergic sensitization

591.name: Steviol glycosides
591.description: Natural sweetening compounds extracted from the Stevia rebaudiana plant, used as high-intensity sweeteners in foods and beverages.
591.benefits: Non-caloric sweetener, does not raise blood glucose, suitable for diabetics and weight management
591.risks: Possible mild gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals, limited data on long-term high-dose consumption

592.name: L-theanine
592.description: A non-protein amino acid commonly found in tea leaves, known for its calming and relaxation effects on the central nervous system.
592.benefits: Promotes relaxation without sedation, may improve focus and cognitive performance
592.risks: None at typical dietary or supplemental intake levels

594.name: Carbonated Purified Water
594.description: Water that has been purified to remove impurities and carbonated by dissolving carbon dioxide gas under pressure. Commonly used as a base in flavored and probiotic beverages.
594.benefits: Hydration, calorie-free base, may aid probiotic delivery
594.risks: Potential dental enamel erosion with excessive consumption of carbonated beverages

595.name: Organic Caffeine
595.description: Organic caffeine is a naturally derived stimulant commonly included in caffeinated flavors to impart alertness and focus. FDA classifies caffeine as Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS) in typical dietary amounts. When labeled organic, caffeine is sourced from organically grown plants without synthetic pesticides. Used within safe consumption limits, organic caffeine has similar effects and safety profile as conventional caffeine.
595.benefits: Increased alertness, improved cognitive performance, enhanced metabolism, fatigue reduction
595.risks: Insomnia, jitteriness, increased heart rate, potential dependence, anxiety in sensitive individuals

601.name: Organic guava natural flavor
601.description: A flavoring ingredient derived from organic guava or its components, used to impart guava taste. Classified as a natural flavor but is often a complex mixture created via extraction, distillation, or fermentation. Considered ultra-processed with limited disclosure on specific chemical composition.
601.benefits: Imparts guava flavor, organic sourcing may reduce synthetic pesticide residue
601.risks: Lack of transparency, potential trace solvents or allergens, ultra-processed, no nutritional value

603.name: Carbonated Water
603.description: Water into which carbon dioxide gas has been dissolved under pressure, creating effervescence.

604.name: Taurine
604.description: A sulfur-containing amino acid often used in energy drinks and supplements for its role in cellular function and osmoregulation.
604.benefits: Supports cellular hydration, antioxidant effects, may improve exercise performance
604.risks: Minor gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses, potential interaction with stimulant compounds

606.name: Sucrose Acetate Isobutyrate
606.description: Sucrose acetate isobutyrate (SAIB) is a synthetic ester used as a stabilizer and emulsifier in food and beverages to maintain uniform dispersion of ingredients.
606.benefits: Enhances stability of emulsions, improves texture and mouthfeel in beverages and food products
606.risks: Potential minor irritant, synthetic processing residues, limited long-term toxicology data

613.name: Beta carotene
613.description: A carotenoid pigment serving as a provitamin A, converted in the body into vitamin A necessary for vision, immune function, and cellular growth.
613.benefits: Provitamin A activity, antioxidant properties, supports vision and immune health
613.risks: Potential increased lung cancer risk in high-dose supplementation among smokers, skin yellowing at excessive intake

616.name: Ascorbic Acid
616.description: Vitamin C, a water-soluble antioxidant used to maintain color and prevent oxidative degradation in food products.

617.name: Magnesium lactate
617.description: A magnesium salt of lactic acid used as an electrolyte to restore magnesium levels and assist in nerve and muscle function.
617.benefits: Provides bioavailable magnesium, supports electrolyte balance, muscle and nerve function
617.risks: Gastrointestinal irritation at high doses, excess intake may cause diarrhea

624.name: Folic acid
624.description: Synthetic form of folate (vitamin B9) used in dietary supplements and food fortification to prevent folate deficiency.
624.benefits: Prevents neural tube defects in pregnancy, supports DNA synthesis and repair, aids red blood cell formation
624.risks: High intake may mask vitamin B12 deficiency, potential concerns for unmetabolized folic acid accumulation

625.name: Riboflavin (Vitamin B2)
625.description: Water-soluble vitamin essential for energy production, cellular function, and metabolism of fats, drugs, and steroids.
625.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, maintains healthy skin and mucous membranes, contributes to redox reactions
625.risks: None at typical dietary or supplemental levels

628.name: Coconut Water
628.description: Clear fluid found inside green coconuts, primarily composed of water with natural sugars, electrolytes, and minor nutrients.
628.benefits: Hydrating, source of electrolytes such as potassium and magnesium
628.risks: Minor risk of gastrointestinal upset in sensitive individuals, natural sugar content

631.name: Potassium sorbate
631.description: Potassium sorbate is a potassium salt of sorbic acid, commonly used as a preservative to inhibit mold, yeast, and fungal growth in food and personal care products.
631.benefits: Effective preservative against molds and yeasts, extends shelf life of products
631.risks: Skin and eye irritation, sensitization in some individuals, potential for respiratory irritation if inhaled as powder

634.name: Magnesium Citrate
634.description: Magnesium citrate is a magnesium salt of citric acid commonly used as a dietary supplement to provide magnesium, an essential mineral important for enzyme function and neuromuscular activity.
634.benefits: Supports magnesium nutritional intake, important for muscle and nerve function, bone health
634.risks: Gastrointestinal irritation, diarrhea at high doses

640.name: Calcium Carbonate
640.description: Calcium carbonate is a common dietary supplement and antacid used to provide calcium and neutralize stomach acid.
640.benefits: Calcium supplementation for bone health, antacid properties to relieve acid indigestion
640.risks: Potential for gastrointestinal discomfort, excessive intake may lead to hypercalcemia or kidney stones

642.name: Phosphoric Acid
642.description: Phosphoric acid is an inorganic acid commonly used as an acidulant in food and beverages to provide sourness and adjust pH.
642.risks: Dental erosion with excessive exposure, potential gastrointestinal irritation at high concentrations

643.name: Citicoline
643.description: Citicoline is a naturally occurring compound (CDP-choline) involved in brain metabolism, often used as a supplement to support cognitive function. In the body, it serves as a precursor for the synthesis of phosphatidylcholine, an important component of brain cell membranes, and is thought to support neurotransmitter production and brain health.
643.benefits: May improve cognitive function, supports memory in aging and mild cognitive impairment, may enhance attention, supports brain phospholipid synthesis
643.risks: Mild gastrointestinal upset, headache, insomnia, rarely can cause hypotension

650.name: Nitrate (as NO₃⁻–N)
650.description: An inorganic ion commonly found in soil, water, and certain foods, nitrate is a nutrient for plants and can be ingested through diet or water. It can be converted to nitrite and other nitrogen compounds in the human body.
650.benefits: Dietary nitrate can contribute to nitric oxide production supporting vascular function
650.risks: Potential formation of nitrosamines under acidic conditions, ingestion toxicity at high levels, methemoglobinemia risk in infants, contamination risk in drinking water

652.name: Calcium lactate
652.description: Calcium salt of lactic acid commonly used as a calcium supplement and food additive to enhance calcium content and as a firming agent.
652.benefits: Provides bioavailable calcium for bone and dental health, food firming agent
652.risks: None at typical dietary or food additive levels

653.name: Sodium hexametaphosphate
653.description: An inorganic polyphosphate salt used as a sequestrant, emulsifier, and to protect flavor in food products by binding metal ions.
653.benefits: Protects flavor by preventing metal-catalyzed oxidation, stabilizes texture and emulsions in foods
653.risks: Potential for phosphorus intake imbalance, gastrointestinal irritation in high amounts, possible contribution to mineral absorption interference

656.name: Calcium Disodium EDTA
656.description: A chelating agent used to bind metal ions, stabilizing formulations and preventing metal-catalyzed oxidation.
656.benefits: Prevents metal ion contamination, enhances stability of formulations, reduces rancidity
656.risks: Potential mild irritation on skin or mucous membranes, low oral toxicity at typical uses, none at usual cosmetic concentrations

658.name: Celtic Sea Salt
658.description: Naturally harvested sea salt from coastal regions, containing sodium chloride with trace minerals.
658.benefits: Essential electrolyte, supports nerve transmission, aids fluid balance
658.risks: Hypertension and cardiovascular risk with excessive intake

659.name: Hydrogen
659.description: Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant element in the universe, often found bound to other elements, most notably as H2O (water). As a food ingredient, it typically refers to hydrogen gas dissolved in water (hydrogen water), promoted for potential antioxidant effects.
659.benefits: Possible antioxidant effects, may help reduce oxidative stress, potential anti-inflammatory properties

660.name: Reverse Osmosis Water
660.description: Water purified by reverse osmosis filtration process, claimed to have altered molecular structure purportedly beneficial but lacks scientific verification.
660.benefits: Purified water free of most contaminants

661.name: Fructose
661.description: A simple monosaccharide sugar found naturally in fruits, honey, and as part of sucrose; commonly used as a sweetener.
661.benefits: Provides sweetening function with lower glycemic index than glucose, occurs naturally in many foods
661.risks: Excessive intake associated with increased risk of insulin resistance, obesity, and metabolic disturbances

662.name: Organic erythritol
662.description: A sugar alcohol used as a low-calorie sweetener. Generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by FDA. Has minimal impact on blood sugar and insulin levels. Fermented by gut bacteria in small amounts, but mostly absorbed and excreted unchanged.
662.benefits: Low-calorie sweetener, does not raise blood glucose or insulin, tooth-friendly, antioxidant properties
662.risks: Possible mild gastrointestinal discomfort in excessive intake, bloating, laxative effect

663.name: Organic lemon juice
663.description: Natural juice extracted from fresh lemons. Commonly used as a flavoring agent and acidulant in foods and beverages.
663.benefits: Source of vitamin C, natural flavoring, supports antioxidant intake
663.risks: Possible oral mucosal irritation in sensitive individuals, photosensitivity with skin exposure in presence of sunlight

664.name: Organic blackberry juice concentrate
664.description: Concentrated fruit juice used for flavor and sweetness; here contains ≤2% of dried blueberries, cellulose, and red cabbage juice extract as colorant.

665.name: Organic amla extract
665.description: Amla extract, derived from the Indian gooseberry (Phyllanthus emblica), is valued for its high vitamin C content and polyphenols, acting as an antioxidant and supporting immune health.
665.benefits: Antioxidant properties, supports immune health, may help regulate blood glucose, potential lipid-lowering effects
665.risks: Possible gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses

666.name: Organic Lemon Balm
666.description: Leaves of the Melissa officinalis plant, commonly used as an herbal ingredient for flavor and fragrance. Contains compounds such as rosmarinic acid and volatile oils.
666.benefits: Flavoring agent, antioxidant properties, mild sedative and anxiolytic effects supported by some studies
666.risks: Possible mild skin irritation or sensitization in some individuals, low ingestion toxicity at typical amounts

667.name: organic schisandra fruit extract
667.description: Schisandra fruit extract is derived from the berries of Schisandra chinensis, a plant traditionally used in East Asian medicine and studied for its adaptogenic, antioxidant, and hepatoprotective properties.
667.benefits: Antioxidant activity, potential liver protective effects, adaptogenic properties, possible cognitive and endurance enhancement
667.risks: Potential interactions with medications, mild gastrointestinal symptoms in sensitive individuals

668.name: Monopotassium phosphate
668.description: Inorganic salt used as an emulsifier, buffering agent, and nutrient source in food products.
668.benefits: Stabilizes emulsions, provides potassium and phosphate minerals, controls pH
668.risks: Possible minor irritation on contact, excessive intake may affect electrolyte balance

669.name: Gum Arabic (Organic Acacia)
669.description: Natural polysaccharide derived from the sap of Acacia trees, commonly used as a stabilizer, emulsifier, and dietary fiber in food products.
669.benefits: Dietary fiber source, stabilizer and emulsifier in foods, low caloric impact
669.risks: Possible rare allergic reactions, minor digestive discomfort in high amounts, low risk of contamination

671.name: Sugar
671.description: Sucrose, a disaccharide carbohydrate used as a sweetener and energy source in food products.
671.benefits: Provides energy, enhances flavor and palatability of foods
671.risks: Excessive intake associated with dental caries, weight gain, increased risk of metabolic syndrome and type 2 diabetes

672.name: Allura Red 40
672.description: Synthetic red azo dye used as a food colorant to provide red coloration.
672.benefits: Improves visual appeal of food products
672.risks: Potential allergen and irritant, possible hyperactivity in children, azo dye hypersensitivity

675.name: Manganese citrate
675.description: Combination of a manganese salt and fruit powder used for mineral supplementation and flavor/color enhancement.
675.benefits: Provides manganese for enzymatic antioxidant defense and cherry juice polyphenols with antioxidant properties
675.risks: Excess manganese intake may lead to neurotoxicity in extreme cases, cherry juice may cause allergic reactions in sensitive individuals

678.name: Apple Juice
678.description: Liquid extract derived from apples, primarily composed of water, sugars, and various organic compounds.
678.benefits: Source of hydration, provides natural sugars and some micronutrients
678.risks: High sugar content, potential dental erosion risk, possible allergen for sensitive individuals

680.name: Blackberry
680.description: Ingredient derived from blackberry fruit, typically used for flavor or color.

683.name: Purified water
683.description: Water that has been mechanically filtered or processed to remove impurities and contaminants.

685.name: Filtered water
685.description: Purified water with impurities and contaminants removed through filtration processes.
685.benefits: Solvent for formulation, hydration, inert carrier

687.name: Natural blueberry pomegranate flavor
687.description: Concentrated flavoring ingredient designed to impart blueberry taste, typically derived from natural or synthetic aromatic compounds used in food and beverages.
687.benefits: Adds blueberry flavor without significant caloric or nutritional contribution
687.risks: Potential for allergenicity or irritation in sensitive individuals, possible presence of undisclosed solvents or chemicals in synthetic versions

688.name: Magnesium oxide
688.description: Inorganic compound commonly used as a dietary magnesium supplement and an antacid. It functions primarily to provide magnesium and neutralize stomach acid.
688.benefits: Provides bioavailable magnesium essential for enzymatic reactions, supports bone health, and neutralizes stomach acid
688.risks: Gastrointestinal irritation at high doses, potential for laxative effect, risk of magnesium overdose in impaired renal function

689.name: Zinc oxide
689.description: Inorganic compound used primarily as a UV filter in sunscreens and as an antimicrobial and skin protectant in topical products.
689.benefits: Effective broad-spectrum UV protection, antimicrobial properties, skin barrier support
689.risks: Potential skin irritation and sensitization in susceptible individuals, inhalation toxicity in nanoparticle form, limited systemic absorption when used topically

692.name: Sodium lactate
692.description: Sodium salt of lactic acid used as a humectant, pH regulator, and preservative in food and cosmetic products.
692.benefits: Moisturizing humectant, pH buffering agent, preserves product stability
692.risks: Irritation in sensitive individuals at high concentrations, minor sensitization potential

700.name: Bacillus coagulans GBI-30 6086
700.description: A spore-forming probiotic bacterium used in dietary supplements and functional foods to support gut microbiota balance.
700.benefits: Supports digestive health, may improve gut microbiota composition, acid and heat resistant for effective delivery
700.risks: Rare cases of infection in immunocompromised individuals, potential allergenicity

701.name: CBD distillate
701.description: CBD distillate is a purified extract from the cannabis plant containing high concentrations of cannabidiol (CBD) and trace amounts of other cannabinoids, terpenes, and plant compounds, with minimal to no THC. It is commonly used for potential therapeutic effects and as an additive in food, beverages, and supplements.
701.benefits: Potential reduction in anxiety, possible anti-inflammatory effects, potential support for chronic pain management, may reduce seizure frequency in certain forms of epilepsy
701.risks: Drug interactions, drowsiness, liver enzyme alterations, gastrointestinal upset, possible product contamination, unknown long-term safety

702.name: Limonene
702.description: A cyclic monoterpene hydrocarbon commonly used as a fragrance and solvent in cleaning products. Derived from citrus oils, it has solvent and scent properties.
702.benefits: Effective natural solvent, pleasant citrus fragrance, biodegradable
702.risks: Skin irritation, potential skin sensitization/allergy, phototoxicity upon oxidation, respiratory irritation at high concentrations

703.name: Maltodextrin
703.description: Maltodextrin is a polysaccharide used as a thickener, filler, or stabilizer in food products. It is derived from starch and is rapidly digestible.
703.benefits: Provides quick source of glucose for energy, improves texture and stability in food products
703.risks: Excessive intake associated with increased blood glucose levels, potential contribution to weight gain and insulin spikes

704.name: Spirulina extract
704.description: Extract derived from Spirulina, a cyanobacterium rich in proteins, vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants used as a dietary supplement ingredient.
704.benefits: Source of proteins, vitamins, minerals, antioxidants
704.risks: Potential for contamination with toxins (microcystins), heavy metals depending on sourcing, allergic reactions, mild gastrointestinal upset

705.name: Allulose
705.description: A low-calorie sweetener structurally similar to fructose, providing sweetness with minimal caloric impact.
705.benefits: Low-calorie sweetener, minimal impact on blood glucose levels compared to sucrose
705.risks: Digestive discomfort at high doses including gas, bloating, diarrhea; limited long-term safety data

707.name: Lion's Mane Extract
707.description: Extract from the mushroom Hericium erinaceus, used as a dietary supplement purported to support cognitive function.
707.benefits: Potential neuroprotective and cognitive support based on preliminary studies
707.risks: Mild allergic reactions, potential gastrointestinal discomfort, unknown long-term safety at high doses

708.name: Reishi Extract
708.description: Extract derived from Ganoderma lucidum mushroom, traditionally used in East Asian medicine. Contains bioactive compounds such as polysaccharides, triterpenoids, and peptidoglycans. Recognized for potential immune-modulating, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant effects. Generally regarded as safe with no FDA approval as a treatment but widely used as a dietary supplement.
708.benefits: Immune modulation, antioxidant properties, anti-inflammatory effects, potential anti-cancer activity, supports general wellness
708.risks: Possible allergenic reactions, rare gastrointestinal discomfort, interactions with immunosuppressive medications

709.name: Watermelon Juice
709.description: Watermelon juice is the liquid extracted from the flesh of the watermelon fruit. It is naturally high in water content, contains vitamins (notably vitamin C and A), minerals, and small amounts of amino acids such as citrulline, and offers hydration and mild antioxidant benefits.
709.benefits: Hydration, source of vitamin C, source of antioxidants, contains citrulline which may benefit exercise performance and vascular health

710.name: Peach Juice Concentrate
710.description: Concentrated juice derived from peaches, used for flavoring and sweetness in foods and beverages.
710.benefits: Provides natural flavor and sweetness, source of some vitamins and antioxidants
710.risks: High sugar content, potential minor allergenicity in sensitive individuals

716.name: Lime Flavor
716.description: Lime flavor typically refers to a blend of natural and/or artificial flavor compounds formulated to mimic the taste of lime, often using solvents, carriers, and processing aids, with little to no nutritional contribution.
716.risks: Lack of transparency, may include solvents or preservatives, potential for ultra-processing, no nutritional value

721.name: Vitamin D3
721.description: Cholecalciferol, a fat-soluble vitamin important for calcium metabolism and bone health.
721.benefits: Supports calcium absorption, bone mineralization, and immune function
721.risks: Toxicity risk at excessive doses leading to hypercalcemia, potential kidney damage

728.name: Pineapple juice
728.description: Juice extracted from pineapple fruit, primarily providing flavor and natural sugars.
728.benefits: Source of vitamins, natural flavor, hydration

730.name: Organic lemon flavor
730.description: Flavoring ingredient derived from lemon components, typically used to impart lemon taste and aroma in foods and beverages. May contain natural lemon oils, extracts, or concentrates.
730.benefits: Provides lemon flavor, enhances taste and aroma, natural origin if certified organic
730.risks: Irritation or sensitization risk for sensitive individuals, risk of allergic reactions in some cases

733.name: Gellan gum
733.description: A polysaccharide used as a gelling and stabilizing agent in food products.
733.benefits: Improves texture and stability in food, acts as a dietary fiber
733.risks: Possible gastrointestinal discomfort at high intake, rare allergic reactions

736.name: Yuzu juice
