736.description: Yuzu juice is the squeezed juice from the yuzu citrus fruit, commonly used in East Asian cuisine for its unique tart and aromatic flavor. It contains vitamin C, antioxidants, and aromatic phytochemicals that may contribute to health and flavor.
736.benefits: Source of vitamin C, antioxidants, potential anti-inflammatory effects
736.risks: Acidic, may cause irritation in sensitive individuals or those with acid reflux

738.name: Zinc sulfate
738.description: An inorganic compound used primarily as a dietary supplement to provide zinc, also used in topical applications and as a micronutrient in agriculture.
738.benefits: Essential trace element, supports immune function, wound healing, enzymatic reactions
738.risks: Irritation risk on skin and mucosa at high concentrations, ingestion toxicity at excessive doses

743.name: Mango juice
743.description: Juice derived from mango fruit, often used as a flavoring or sweetener in beverages and foods. Contains natural sugars, vitamins, and phytochemicals.
743.benefits: Source of vitamins (notably vitamin C), antioxidants, and natural flavor
743.risks: Excess sugar intake, potential for dental erosion if consumed excessively

747.name: Potassium carbonate
747.description: Inorganic compound used as a raising agent to increase pH and produce carbon dioxide for leavening in baked goods.
747.benefits: Leavening agent improving texture and volume in food products
747.risks: Irritation risk at high concentrations, ingestion toxicity in large amounts

751.name: Guarana seed extract
751.description: Extract derived from guarana seeds standardized to contain 50% caffeine. Primarily used for stimulant and cognitive enhancing effects.
751.benefits: Central nervous system stimulant, improved alertness and focus, potential cognitive enhancement, mild metabolic stimulation
751.risks: Caffeine-related risks including nervousness, insomnia, increased heart rate, potential for dependence, irritant potential at high doses

752.name: Niacin (Vitamin B3)
752.description: Water-soluble vitamin involved in energy metabolism and DNA repair.
752.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, aids DNA repair
752.risks: High doses can cause skin flushing, liver toxicity

753.name: Pantothenic Acid (Vitamin B5)
753.description: Water-soluble B vitamin essential for synthesis of coenzyme A, involved in energy metabolism and synthesis of fatty acids, steroids, and acetylcholine.
753.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, skin health, and wound healing
753.risks: Rare allergic reactions and mild gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses

755.name: Cobalamin (Vitamin B12)
755.description: Water-soluble vitamin essential for red blood cell formation, neurological function, and DNA synthesis.
755.benefits: Supports red blood cell production, neurological health, and DNA synthesis
755.risks: None at typical dietary or supplemental doses

758.name: Calcium citrate
758.description: Calcium citrate is a calcium salt of citric acid commonly used as a dietary calcium supplement to support bone health and calcium intake.
758.benefits: Provides bioavailable calcium for bone mineralization and maintenance
758.risks: Gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses, potential interaction with certain medications

764.name: Probiotic cultures
764.description: Probiotic cultures are live microorganisms, usually specific strains of bacteria like Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium, added to foods or supplements with the intent to confer a beneficial effect on the host's gut microbiota when consumed in adequate amounts.
764.benefits: Support for gut microbiota balance, may improve digestion, can reduce symptoms of some digestive disorders, potential support for immune function
764.risks: Mild digestive discomfort, risk of infection in immunocompromised individuals, transient bloating

768.name: Sparkling filtered water
768.description: Filtered water that has been carbonated with dissolved carbon dioxide gas to create effervescence. Generally recognized as safe and hydrating with no nutritional calories or additives.
768.benefits: Hydration, calorie-free, refreshing alternative to still water

772.name: Organic yerba mate extract
772.description: Organic yerba mate extract is derived from the leaves of Ilex paraguariensis, a South American plant. It contains caffeine, polyphenols, saponins, and vitamins, and is used for its stimulant and antioxidant properties in foods and supplements.
772.benefits: Antioxidant activity, enhanced alertness, improved lipid metabolism, anti-inflammatory potential
772.risks: Caffeine-related side effects, possible increased cancer risk with heavy consumption of traditional hot infusions, gastrointestinal irritation

773.name: Organic pomegranate juice concentrate
773.description: A concentrated form of juice derived from organic pomegranates, retaining many of the fruit's antioxidants and polyphenols. Generally recognized as safe for consumption and may provide nutritional benefits similar to fresh pomegranate juice but with higher sugar concentration per volume.
773.benefits: Rich in antioxidants, polyphenols, may support cardiovascular health, anti-inflammatory properties
773.risks: High sugar content, potential for contributing to caloric excess if consumed in large amounts

776.name: Artificial flavors
776.description: Synthetic chemical compounds designed to mimic natural flavors in food products.
776.benefits: Enhance taste, allow consistent flavor profiles in processed foods
776.risks: Potential allergenicity, processing contaminants, lack of nutritional value, possible irritant or sensitizer effects

777.name: Vodka
777.description: Distilled alcoholic beverage typically containing 40% ethanol; here at 12% concentration in a diluted form.
777.risks: Alcohol ingestion toxicity, CNS depression, impaired motor function, excessive consumption risk

778.name: Tartaric acid
778.description: A naturally occurring organic acid commonly used as an antioxidant and acidity regulator in food products.
778.benefits: Antioxidant properties, acidity regulation in foods, enhances shelf life
778.risks: Irritation potential at high concentrations, possible digestive discomfort if consumed in excess

780.name: Nitrogen
780.description: Inert diatomic gas that makes up approximately 78% of Earth's atmosphere. Used in cleaning products mainly as a propellant or inert atmosphere agent.
780.benefits: Non-toxic, non-flammable, chemically inert, stabilizes formulations, reduces oxidation
780.risks: Asphyxiation in confined or poorly ventilated areas due to displacement of oxygen

781.name: Tapioca starch
781.description: A carbohydrate extracted from the cassava root, primarily used as a thickening and stabilizing agent in foods and industrial products.
781.benefits: Gluten-free thickener, stabilizes texture, easily digestible carbohydrate source

789.name: Vitamin C
789.description: Water-soluble vitamin important for antioxidant protection, collagen synthesis, and immune function.
789.benefits: Antioxidant, supports collagen synthesis, aids immune response
789.risks: None at typical dietary or topical use levels, high doses may cause gastrointestinal upset

790.name: Vitamin D
790.description: Fat-soluble vitamin essential for calcium homeostasis and bone metabolism.
790.benefits: Supports bone health, calcium absorption, immune function
790.risks: Toxicity from excessive supplementation causing hypercalcemia, limited risk at typical dietary levels

791.name: Magnesium Glycinate
791.description: A chelated form of magnesium bound to glycine used as a dietary supplement to increase magnesium intake.
791.benefits: Enhanced magnesium bioavailability compared to other forms, supports muscle and nerve function, aids in magnesium deficiency management
791.risks: Mild gastrointestinal upset in high doses, potential laxative effect

798.name: Soybean oil
798.description: Edible oil extracted from soybeans, rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids, primarily used as a cooking oil and food ingredient.
798.benefits: Source of essential fatty acids, provides energy in diet
798.risks: High omega-6 fatty acid content, oxidative instability at high heat, potential hexane solvent residue from processing, possible estrogenic effects from minor soy protein contamination

803.name: Magnesium phosphate
803.description: An inorganic salt used as a dietary supplement to provide magnesium and phosphate essential minerals.
803.benefits: Provides magnesium essential for muscle and nerve function, bone health, and energy metabolism; supports phosphate balance important for ATP and cellular function
803.risks: None at typical dietary amounts, excessive intake may cause gastrointestinal discomfort or diarrhea

804.name: Sodium Ascorbate
804.description: Sodium ascorbate is a sodium salt of ascorbic acid (vitamin C) used as a vitamin supplement and antioxidant additive in foods and supplements.
804.benefits: Antioxidant, supports collagen synthesis, essential vitamin C source
804.risks: None at typical intake levels, high doses may cause gastrointestinal discomfort

805.name: Chromium polynicotinate
805.description: Chromium polynicotinate is a chemical compound consisting of the essential mineral chromium bound to niacin (vitamin B3) and is used as a dietary supplement to support glucose metabolism and potentially improve insulin sensitivity.
805.benefits: May improve glucose metabolism, possible support for insulin sensitivity, may aid glucose homeostasis in deficient individuals
805.risks: Possible gastrointestinal upset, potential kidney or liver effects at high doses, drug interactions

807.name: Sodium molybdate
807.description: Inorganic compound used as a source of molybdenum in dietary supplements and industrial applications.
807.benefits: Essential trace mineral supporting enzyme function in sulfur and nitrogen metabolism
807.risks: Ingestion toxicity at high doses, potential heavy metal contamination

822.name: Soy protein isolate
822.description: Highly processed plant protein extracted from soybeans, used to increase protein content in foods.
822.benefits: High protein content, complete amino acid profile, supports muscle protein synthesis
822.risks: Hexane extraction residues, potential endocrine disruption due to isoflavones, allergenicity, ultra-processed

823.name: Chromium chloride
823.description: Chromium chloride is a supplemental form of the trace mineral chromium, often used to fortify foods or dietary supplements, and involved in carbohydrate and lipid metabolism in the human body.
823.benefits: Supports glucose metabolism, essential trace mineral
823.risks: Potential toxicity at high doses, possible allergic reactions, unknown long-term safety of supplementation

835.name: Thiamine mononitrate (Vitamin B1)
835.description: Synthetic form of vitamin B1 used as a dietary supplement and food fortification agent to prevent or treat thiamin deficiency.
835.benefits: Prevents and treats thiamin deficiency, supports energy metabolism, nervous system function
835.risks: Low toxicity at typical dietary levels, rare allergic reactions possible

838.name: Potassium hydroxide
838.description: An inorganic compound used as a pH regulator and neutralizing agent in food products and cosmetics.
838.benefits: Effective pH regulator and neutralizer, facilitates texture and stability in formulations
838.risks: Corrosive causing skin and eye irritation in concentrated form, potential inhalation irritant as dust or aerosol, regulatory restrictions on concentration in consumer products

839.name: Ferrous sulfate
839.description: An iron salt commonly used as a dietary supplement to treat or prevent iron deficiency anemia.
839.benefits: Corrects and prevents iron deficiency, supports red blood cell production, essential mineral supplement
839.risks: Gastrointestinal irritation, constipation, diarrhea, nausea, risk of iron overdose especially in children

858.name: Pomegranate
858.description: Edible fruit known for its seeds and juice, containing antioxidants including polyphenols and vitamin C.
858.benefits: Antioxidant properties, source of vitamins and polyphenols, supports nutrient intake
858.risks: Rare allergenic potential, none at typical dietary levels

868.name: Organic Cordyceps mushroom
868.description: Cordyceps is a genus of fungi traditionally used in Chinese medicine, known for containing compounds such as cordycepin and polysaccharides that may modulate immune response and enhance physical performance.
868.benefits: May support immune function, may improve exercise performance, potential antioxidant activity
868.risks: Mild digestive upset, possible allergenic reactions, drug interactions

886.name: Cinnamon
886.description: Spice obtained from the inner bark of Cinnamomum trees, used for flavoring and aroma.
886.benefits: Flavoring agent, antimicrobial properties at low concentrations
886.risks: Irritant and sensitizer potential, especially for skin and mucous membranes; contains coumarin which may be hepatotoxic in high doses

888.name: Strawberry puree
888.description: Blend of crushed or blended whole strawberries, containing natural sugars, fibers, and nutrients from the fruit.
888.benefits: Source of dietary fiber, vitamin C, antioxidants, and natural flavor
888.risks: Allergen potential in sensitive individuals, sugar content contributes to caloric intake

890.name: Rosemary extract
890.description: Extract derived from rosemary leaves used primarily as a natural antioxidant to improve product freshness and shelf life.
890.benefits: Antioxidant properties that help preserve product freshness, natural preservative substitute
890.risks: Possible skin sensitization or allergic reaction in some individuals, minor irritant risk

894.name: Chromium picolinate
894.description: A chemical compound used as a dietary supplement to provide the essential trace mineral chromium, which is involved in macronutrient metabolism and insulin function.
894.benefits: Supports glucose metabolism, may improve insulin sensitivity, trace mineral nutritional source
894.risks: Potential mild renal toxicity at high doses, possible oxidative stress, limited evidence of adverse endocrine effects

899.name: Trimagnesium citrate
899.description: A magnesium salt of citric acid used as a dietary supplement to increase magnesium levels and sometimes as a mild laxative.
899.benefits: Magnesium source supporting muscle and nerve function, electrolyte balance
899.risks: Laxative effect at high doses, gastrointestinal discomfort

900.name: HFPO-DA (PFAS)
900.description: Hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (HFPO-DA) is a per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS), commonly known by the trade name GenX. It is a synthetic fluorinated chemical used as a processing aid in fluoropolymer manufacture. PFAS compounds are persistent environmental pollutants with bioaccumulative properties and potential toxicity.
900.risks: Environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, potential toxicity, endocrine disruption, liver toxicity, carcinogenic potential

902.name: High Fructose Corn Syrup
902.description: A sweetener derived from corn starch containing variable amounts of fructose and glucose, used to enhance sweetness and preserve moisture in foods.
902.benefits: Provides sweetness and energy, improves texture and shelf-life in processed foods
902.risks: Metabolic effects including insulin resistance, contribution to obesity and related disorders with excessive intake

906.name: L-malic acid
906.description: L-malic acid is a naturally occurring organic acid found in fruits like apples. It is used as a food additive to add sourness and as a preservative. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used in typical food amounts.
906.benefits: Contributes to energy production in the Krebs cycle, enhances flavor, natural preservative, may improve skin hydration when used topically
906.risks: Gastrointestinal irritation at high doses, tooth enamel erosion with excessive exposure

907.name: Potassium phosphate
907.description: An inorganic salt used as a food additive, buffering agent, and acidity regulator in beverages and processed foods.
907.benefits: Helps maintain acid-base balance in foods, stabilizes pH, can act as an electrolyte source
907.risks: Excess intake may affect electrolyte balance, possible gastrointestinal irritation at high doses

909.name: Zinc Citrate
909.description: Chelated mineral salts used as dietary supplements to provide bioavailable zinc and manganese.
909.benefits: Essential trace minerals, support enzymatic reactions, antioxidant functions
909.risks: Excessive intake may cause gastrointestinal irritation, mineral imbalance

917.name: Organic Monk Fruit Extract
917.description: Monk fruit extract is a natural sweetener derived from the luo han guo fruit. It contains mogrosides, which are intensely sweet compounds used as sugar substitutes. Monk fruit extract is often used for its low-calorie sweetening properties without significant impact on blood glucose levels. The FDA has granted monk fruit extract Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS) status.
917.benefits: Calorie-free sugar alternative, does not raise blood glucose, low glycemic index
917.risks: Possible mild gastrointestinal upset in sensitive individuals, ultra-processed, limited long-term studies

929.name: Organic lion's mane
929.description: Organic lion's mane refers to the fruiting body of the Hericium erinaceus mushroom, grown without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. It is traditionally used in Asian medicine and contains bioactive compounds such as hericenones and erinacines, which are studied for nootropic and neuroprotective effects.
929.benefits: May support cognitive function, potential neuroprotective properties, may reduce mild anxiety and depressive symptoms, antioxidant activity
929.risks: Allergic reactions (rare), potential medication interactions (rare), insufficient long-term safety data

943.name: Green tea leaf extract
943.description: Concentrated extract from green tea leaves containing polyphenols such as catechins, primarily used for antioxidant properties.
943.benefits: Antioxidant activity, potential free radical scavenging
943.risks: Potential mild skin irritation or sensitization in topical use, possible hepatotoxicity in very high doses orally, caffeine-related effects

951.name: Ashwagandha root extract
951.description: Extract from Ashwagandha root (Withania somnifera), standardized to contain 3.5% withanolides, biologically active steroidal lactones.
951.benefits: Adaptogenic properties, supports stress response modulation
951.risks: Potential for mild gastrointestinal irritation, possible allergenicity, interaction with thyroid or immunomodulatory medications

980.name: Organic green tea extract
980.description: Concentrated extracts from green tea leaves, rich in polyphenols such as catechins including epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG). Commonly used for antioxidant properties.
980.benefits: Antioxidant activity, vascular support, potential neuroprotective effects
980.risks: Potential for liver toxicity at high doses, possible mild skin irritation, caffeine content may cause sensitivity

988.name: Organic turmeric extract
988.description: Organic turmeric extract is a concentrated form of turmeric root, standardized for curcuminoids, the bioactive compounds responsible for its yellow color and anti-inflammatory properties.
988.benefits: Anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, may support joint health, may improve metabolic health
988.risks: Possible gastrointestinal upset at high doses, may interact with anticoagulant medications

989.name: Organic spinach powder
989.description: Dehydrated and powdered form of organic spinach, retaining much of the nutritional profile of fresh spinach. Recognized as a nutrient-dense vegetable source, spinach powder is generally safe for consumption and may be used as a supplement or ingredient to enhance nutritional content. It is not specifically regulated by the FDA but falls under general food safety regulations for organic produce.
989.benefits: Rich source of vitamins A, C, K, folate, iron, antioxidants, dietary fiber
989.risks: Oxalate content may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals

994.name: Natural vanilla flavor
994.description: Complex mixture of aromatic compounds extracted from vanilla beans or synthesized to mimic vanilla aroma, used as a flavoring agent.
994.benefits: Provides vanilla flavoring enhancing palatability of foods
994.risks: Potential allergenicity, possible minor skin or respiratory sensitization, lacks transparency in exact composition

995.name: Stevia extract
995.description: Natural sweetener derived from the leaves of the Stevia rebaudiana plant, primarily composed of steviol glycosides.
995.benefits: Non-caloric sweetener, does not raise blood glucose or insulin levels, useful for sugar reduction
995.risks: Potential allergenicity in sensitive individuals, possible mild gastrointestinal effects in high doses

1005.name: Lemon Balm Extract
1005.description: Extract derived from leaves of Melissa officinalis (lemon balm), commonly used for flavoring and potential soothing effects. The extract referenced is from certified organic cultivation.
1005.benefits: Natural flavoring agent, mild calming properties, antioxidant content
1005.risks: Allergic sensitization in sensitive individuals, possible mild skin irritation

1012.name: Heterotrophic Plate Count
1012.description: A count of all carbon-consuming bacteria in water, the vast majority of which are harmless
1012.risks: Potential endocrine disruptor; long-term exposure is linked to hormonal disruption, reproductive toxicity, and developmental effects

1031.name: Pectin
1031.description: A soluble dietary fiber commonly extracted from citrus fruits and apples, used primarily as a gelling agent and stabilizer in food products.
1031.benefits: Dietary fiber source, supports digestive health, acts as a thickening and gelling agent

1034.name: Baking soda
1034.description: Sodium bicarbonate, a white crystalline powder commonly used as a leavening agent in baking, odor neutralizer, and mild abrasive.
1034.benefits: Leavening agent in baking, odor neutralizing, mild abrasive for cleaning
1034.risks: Irritation to eyes and mucous membranes on direct contact, ingestion in large amounts may cause electrolyte imbalance

1055.name: Natural Spring Water
1055.description: Natural spring water is water sourced from underground formations and emerges naturally to the surface. It typically contains mineral content specific to its source and undergoes minimal processing to preserve the original mineral composition.
1055.benefits: Source of hydration, contains naturally occurring minerals, generally free from added chemicals
1055.risks: May contain trace minerals or contaminants, possible microbial presence if untreated, vulnerable to environmental pollution

1058.name: White Grape Juice Concentrate
1058.description: Concentrated juice derived from white grapes, primarily composed of sugars, organic acids, and phenolic compounds.
1058.benefits: Contains natural antioxidants including polyphenols, potential mild antioxidant activity
1058.risks: High sugar content contributing to calorie intake and dental caries risk

1060.name: Yellow 6
1060.description: Synthetic azo dye (also known as Sunset Yellow FCF) used as a colorant in foods, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals.
1060.benefits: Colorant to improve product appearance and consumer appeal
1060.risks: Potential allergenic reactions, behavioral effects in sensitive children, regulatory restrictions in some countries

1061.name: Ester gum
1061.description: A food additive used as a weighting agent and emulsifier to stabilize flavor oils in beverages and food products.
1061.risks: None reported at typical use levels

1073.name: Alkaline water
1073.description: Alkaline water is water that has been ionized to increase its pH above neutral, often through electrolysis or by adding minerals. It is claimed to offer various health benefits, but scientific evidence supporting these claims is limited.
1073.risks: May contain added minerals or contaminants, potential for altering stomach acidity, misleading health claims

1080.name: Preservatives
1080.description: A broad category of chemical agents added to cleaning products to inhibit bacterial and fungal growth, enhancing product shelf-life. Includes diverse chemical classes such as isothiazolinones, parabens, formaldehyde releasers, and others.
1080.benefits: Prevents microbial contamination, extends product shelf life, maintains product safety and efficacy
1080.risks: Skin sensitization, contact allergy, eye irritation, toxicity varies by specific preservative, some restricted under EU and EPA regulations, potential environmental toxicity

1082.name: Blueberry juice from concentrate
1082.description: Blueberry juice from concentrate is made by removing water from blueberry juice and later reconstituting it with water, resulting in some loss of phytonutrients and antioxidants compared to fresh juice. It provides some vitamins and anthocyanins but at reduced levels due to processing.
1082.benefits: Source of vitamin C, provides some anthocyanins, contains trace minerals
1082.risks: Reduced antioxidant content, potential added sugars during reconstitution, loss of phytonutrients during processing

1085.name: Niacinamide (Vitamin B3)
1085.description: Water-soluble vitamin B3 form used in nutrition and topical formulations for cellular metabolism and skin barrier support.
1085.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, skin barrier function, and cellular repair
1085.risks: Rare skin irritation or sensitization with topical use, high oral doses may cause flushing or liver toxicity

1115.name: Organic sugar cane
1115.description: Organic sugar cane is a plant-derived sweetener produced from organically grown sugar cane, free from synthetic pesticides and fertilizers. It is minimally processed compared to refined white sugar but remains a source of sucrose, providing simple carbohydrates and energy. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA and commonly used to sweeten food and beverages.
1115.risks: High glycemic index, may contribute to tooth decay, excess consumption linked to metabolic syndrome, weight gain, diabetes risk

1137.name: Potassium Salt
1137.description: Potassium salts are salts of potassium used primarily as salt substitutes to reduce sodium intake. They contribute potassium ions essential for cellular function.
1137.benefits: Lower sodium alternative, supports electrolyte balance, helps maintain normal blood pressure
1137.risks: Hyperkalemia risk in patients with kidney impairment or on potassium-sparing medications

1160.name: Sparkling Water
1160.description: Water infused with carbon dioxide gas under pressure, creating effervescence.
1160.risks: Mild dental enamel erosion risk compared to still water

1162.name: Natural Lemon Flavor
1162.description: Extracted flavor compounds derived from lemon fruit, typically used to impart citrus aroma and taste in food products.
1162.benefits: Provides citrus flavor, enhances sensory appeal
1162.risks: Irritation or sensitization in sensitive individuals, potential presence of allergens or trace contaminants, ultra-processed additive

1163.name: Natural Lime Flavor
1163.description: A composite flavor ingredient containing maltodextrin, sugar, lime oil, lime juice concentrate, sunflower lecithin, gum arabic, and silicon dioxide used to impart lime flavor in food products.
1163.benefits: Flavor enhancement, improves sensory appeal of foods
1163.risks: Potential minor irritation or sensitization from lime oil, ultra-processed components (maltodextrin, sugar), mild exposure to sunflower lecithin (hexane extraction potential), silicon dioxide as processed additive

1220.name: Pure Cane Sugar
1220.description: Sucrose derived from sugar cane, commonly used as a sweetener in foods and beverages.
1220.risks: Excessive intake associated with weight gain, dental caries, metabolic effects

1221.name: Vitamins C (Ascorbic Acid)
1221.description: Vitamin C, or ascorbic acid, is a water-soluble vitamin essential for collagen synthesis, antioxidant protection, and immune function. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used within recommended dietary amounts.
1221.benefits: Antioxidant, supports immune health, aids collagen formation, enhances iron absorption
1221.risks: Gastrointestinal upset at high doses, potential kidney stone risk in susceptible individuals

1243.name: Organic Honey
1243.description: Natural sweetener produced by bees from floral nectar, containing sugars, trace enzymes, and antioxidants.
1243.benefits: Provides sweetness, contains antioxidants, may have minor antimicrobial properties
1243.risks: Possible allergen, risk of infant botulism if consumed by infants under 1 year

1268.name: Pyridoxal 5'-Phosphate (Vitamin B6)
1268.description: A phosphorylated form of vitamin B6 (pyridoxine phosphate), involved as a coenzyme in amino acid metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.
1268.benefits: Essential coenzyme in amino acid metabolism, supports neurotransmitter synthesis and nervous system function

1279.name: Organic apple juice
1279.description: Apple juice is a liquid extracted from apples, used as a flavoring or sweetening ingredient. Organic certification indicates cultivation without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers.
1279.benefits: Provides natural flavor and sugars, source of some micronutrients and antioxidants
1279.risks: High sugar content, potential for dental caries with excessive consumption

1285.name: Organic Lemon Juice Concentrate
1285.description: Concentrated form of lemon juice derived from organically grown lemons, used primarily for flavoring and acidity control.
1285.benefits: Provides natural citrus flavor, source of vitamin C, used as a natural preservative and acidity regulator
1285.risks: Acidic irritation to skin or mucous membranes in high concentrations, potential allergen

1290.name: Organic coconut water concentrate
1290.description: Concentrated coconut water which contains organic acids such as citric acid; used primarily for flavoring and hydration.
1290.benefits: Provides electrolytes such as potassium, supports hydration
1290.risks: Potential mild irritation in sensitive individuals due to acidity, possible allergen in rare cases

1292.name: Orange juice concentrate
1292.description: Fruit juice concentrated by removing water, used as a flavoring and sweetener in foods and beverages.
1292.benefits: Source of vitamin C, provides flavor and nutrients from oranges
1292.risks: High sugar content, potential for dental erosion with excessive intake

1295.name: Organic green tea caffeine
1295.description: Organic green tea caffeine is caffeine naturally extracted from organically grown Camellia sinensis leaves. In the body, caffeine acts as a central nervous system stimulant, increasing alertness and temporarily reducing fatigue.
1295.benefits: Enhanced cognitive performance, improved alertness, potential antioxidant effects, increased metabolic rate
1295.risks: Insomnia, anxiety, increased heart rate, potential interaction with medications, gastrointestinal upset

1297.name: Organic lime extract
1297.description: Organic lime extract is derived from organically grown lime fruit and typically contains concentrated flavor compounds, antioxidants, and small amounts of vitamins such as vitamin C. It offers citrus aroma and tartness when used in food products.
1297.benefits: Contains flavonoids, provides vitamin C, antioxidant properties

1298.name: Modified Food Starch
1298.description: Starch chemically or physically altered to improve texture, stability, and shelf life in processed foods.
1298.benefits: Improves texture and stability in food products, enhances shelf life
1298.risks: Ultra-processed ingredient, potential allergen for sensitive individuals, may contain residual processing agents

1299.name: Blue 1
1299.description: Synthetic blue dye (FD&C Blue No. 1, Brilliant Blue FCF) used as a colorant in foods, drugs, and cosmetics.
1299.benefits: Provides vibrant blue color for consumer acceptability and product identification
1299.risks: Potential allergen, hypersensitivity reactions in susceptible individuals, concern about behavioral effects in children, possible contamination with heavy metals depending on source quality

1316.name: Potassium Benzoate (Preservative)
1316.description: Potassium benzoate is a synthetic preservative used to inhibit the growth of mold, yeast, and some bacteria in acidic foods and beverages, thereby extending shelf life.
1316.risks: Potential for benzene formation in presence of vitamin C, possible mild allergen, ultra-processed additive, no nutritional value

1320.name: Sodium Benzoate
1320.description: Sodium benzoate is a widely used preservative in food, beverages, and cosmetics to inhibit microbial growth and extend shelf life.
1320.benefits: Antimicrobial preservative, extends product shelf life, prevents spoilage
1320.risks: Irritant in high concentrations, potential to form benzene (a carcinogen) when combined with ascorbic acid, regulatory limits restrict maximum allowed concentrations in foods

1322.name: White tea extract
1322.description: Extract derived from white tea (Camellia sinensis) leaves, containing polyphenols and other bioactive compounds, used for flavor and antioxidant properties.
1322.benefits: Antioxidant activity, potential anti-aging effects for skin, natural flavoring agent
1322.risks: Irritant potential in sensitive skin on topical use, possible mild sensitization in rare cases, caffeine content may cause mild stimulant effects if ingested in large amounts

1323.name: Purified sparkling water
1323.description: Water that has been purified to remove contaminants and infused with carbon dioxide gas to create carbonation. Generally recognized as safe and commonly consumed as a hydrating beverage.
1323.benefits: Hydration, calorie-free, alternative to sugary carbonated drinks

1339.name: Watermelon juice concentrate
1339.description: Concentrated form of watermelon juice typically used as a flavoring or sweetener ingredient in foods and beverages.
1339.benefits: Provides natural flavor and sweetness, contains antioxidants like lycopene from watermelon
1339.risks: High sugar content contributing to caloric intake, potential for minor allergenicity

1341.name: Added Electrolytes (Potassium bicarbonate)
1341.description: Potassium bicarbonate is an inorganic salt used to supply potassium, an essential electrolyte involved in muscle function, nerve signaling, and acid-base balance. In food products, it is added to support hydration or as a buffering agent.
1341.benefits: Supports electrolyte balance, may help maintain acid-base equilibrium, supports nerve and muscle function
1341.risks: Potential hyperkalemia in individuals with kidney disease, gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses

1343.name: Added Electrolytes (Calcium chloride)
1343.description: Calcium chloride is an inorganic salt used to fortify foods and beverages with calcium and enhance electrolyte content. It dissociates into calcium and chloride ions in the body, supporting normal muscle, nerve, and metabolic function.
1343.benefits: Contributes to dietary calcium intake, helps maintain electrolyte balance, supports muscle and nerve function
1343.risks: Gastrointestinal irritation at high doses, hypercalcemia risk in sensitive individuals, may impart a salty or bitter taste

1345.name: Vapor distilled water
1345.description: Water purified by vapor distillation, removing impurities and minerals. Commonly used in food and cosmetic formulations. Generally recognized as safe (GRAS) for consumption and topical use.
1345.benefits: Pure hydration source, free from contaminants and minerals, safe for consumption and use in formulations

1347.name: Organic Raspberry Flavor
1347.description: Organic raspberry flavor is a concentrated extract or blend derived from organic raspberries and/or natural sources, created to impart raspberry taste. While the organic certification generally restricts certain synthetic solvents and additives, the ingredient still involves chemical extraction, concentration, and often lacks transparency regarding its full composition. It is commonly used in processed foods and beverages for flavor enhancement.
1347.risks: Lack of transparency, may contain undisclosed carrier agents, ultra-processed, no nutritional value

1500.name: Maltitol
1500.description: Maltitol is a sugar alcohol used as a low-calorie sweetener, providing sweetness similar to sucrose with fewer calories.
1500.benefits: Provides sweetness with lower calories than sugar, does not elevate blood glucose as much as sugar
1500.risks: Digestive discomfort, laxative effects at high intake

1502.name: Collagen peptides
1502.description: Collagen peptides are short chains of amino acids derived from collagen protein, typically sourced from animal connective tissue. They are used in food and supplements for their potential to support skin elasticity, joint health, and connective tissue function.
1502.benefits: May support skin hydration and elasticity, may improve joint health, may promote bone health

1509.name: Sweetener Maltitol
1509.description: A sugar alcohol used as a low-calorie sweetener in food products, derived from hydrogenated starch hydrolysates.
1509.benefits: Lower glycemic response than sugar, reduced calorie sweetener
1509.risks: Gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses, laxative effects

1531.name: Aroma
1531.description: Aroma refers to flavoring substances added to products to impart a particular smell or taste. It often includes chemically extracted compounds and can be natural or synthetic.
1531.risks: Potential irritant or sensitizer depending on compounds, lack of transparency, possible presence of solvents or trace contaminants

1654.name: Natural Vanilla Flavouring
1654.description: Flavoring derived from vanilla beans or natural extracts used to impart vanilla aroma and taste in foods and beverages.
1654.benefits: Provides characteristic vanilla flavor and aroma, enhances palatability of food products
1654.risks: Potential for allergenic reactions in sensitive individuals, possible exposure to trace contaminants depending on extraction and production methods, minimal irritation risk

1788.name: Vitamin E
1788.description: Fat-soluble antioxidant vitamin found in various foods and supplements, used to prevent oxidative damage to cells.
1788.benefits: Antioxidant properties, supports cellular protection from oxidative stress
1788.risks: High dose supplementation may increase bleeding risk, potential for pro-oxidant effects at excessive levels

1872.name: Niacin
1872.description: Water-soluble B-vitamin (vitamin B3) involved in energy metabolism and cellular function.
1872.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, supports skin and nervous system health, aids DNA repair
1872.risks: High doses can cause flushing, gastrointestinal upset, liver toxicity

1875.name: Riboflavin
1875.description: Water-soluble vitamin B2 used as a food colorant and nutrient supplement.
1875.risks: Rare allergic reactions in sensitive individuals

1891.name: Palm Oil
1891.description: Edible oil derived from the fruit of the oil palm tree, rich in saturated and monounsaturated fats.
1891.benefits: Stable cooking oil due to saturated fat content, source of vitamin E
1891.risks: High saturated fat content associated with cardiovascular disease risk if consumed in excess, environmental concerns in large-scale cultivation

1989.name: Orange
1989.description: Citrus fruit widely used for flavoring and nutritional content including vitamin C and flavonoids.
1989.benefits: Source of vitamin C, antioxidants, flavoring agent
1989.risks: Irritation risk for sensitive skin or allergic individuals, pesticide residues possible if not organic

1990.name: Lemon
1990.description: Lemon is the fruit of Citrus limon, commonly used for flavoring and fragrance due to its acidic juice and aromatic peel.
1990.benefits: Flavoring agent, fragrance, source of citric acid
1990.risks: Skin irritation and photosensitivity in topical use at higher concentrations, possible allergen

1993.name: Apple
1993.description: Edible fruit from Malus domestica, primarily composed of water, carbohydrates (mainly sugars and fiber), vitamins, and antioxidants.
1993.benefits: Provides dietary fiber, vitamins (such as vitamin C), antioxidants, supports digestive health
1993.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, pesticide residue if not properly washed, potential fructose intolerance issues in some

1998.name: Carrot
1998.description: Root vegetable commonly consumed for its carotenoid content and dietary fiber.
1998.benefits: Source of beta-carotene, vitamins, dietary fiber, antioxidants

2001.name: Raspberry
2001.description: Fruit ingredient derived from Rubus idaeus, commonly used for flavoring and natural coloring.
2001.benefits: Natural flavoring, source of antioxidants and vitamins in dietary context
2001.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, possible pesticide residues if not organic

2013.name: Coriander
2013.description: Herb derived from Coriandrum sativum seeds, often used as a spice or flavoring agent.
2013.risks: Possible skin sensitization or allergic reactions in some individuals

2024.name: Natural Watermelon Flavor
2024.description: Extracted flavor compounds derived from watermelon, used to impart watermelon taste in food and beverages.
2024.benefits: Provides watermelon flavoring for palatability and sensory appeal
2024.risks: Potential for allergens, may contain trace solvents or processing residues, ultra-processed ingredient

2066.name: L-Tryptophan
2066.description: An essential amino acid required for protein synthesis and precursor to neurotransmitters such as serotonin and melatonin.
2066.benefits: Supports protein synthesis, precursor to serotonin and melatonin, may aid mood regulation and sleep
2066.risks: Allergic reactions or sensitization in rare cases, risk of eosinophilia-myalgia syndrome from contaminated supplements, none at typical dietary intake

2070.name: Organic Agave Syrup
2070.description: A natural sweetener derived from the agave plant, composed primarily of fructose and glucose.
2070.benefits: Sweetening agent, provides sugars for energy
2070.risks: High fructose content associated with excessive caloric intake, potential weight gain with overconsumption

2096.name: Natural Grapefruit Essence
2096.description: Natural grapefruit essence is typically a volatile aromatic extract obtained from the peel or juice of grapefruits, used to impart flavor and aroma to foods and beverages. It contains concentrated grapefruit-derived compounds but lacks significant nutritional value.
2096.risks: Potential allergen, lack of transparency in processing, may contain trace solvents or carriers, no nutritional value

2101.name: D-Alpha-Tocopherol Acetate
2101.description: D-Alpha-Tocopherol Acetate is a synthetic ester form of vitamin E commonly used as a dietary supplement and antioxidant in food products. It is converted to the biologically active form of vitamin E in the body, supporting cellular membranes and acting as a free radical scavenger.
2101.benefits: Antioxidant activity, supports immune function, protects cell membranes
2101.risks: Digestive upset at high doses, potential anticoagulant effect at high intake, possible interaction with anticoagulant medications

2102.name: Beta-carotene
2102.description: A carotenoid pigment functioning as a provitamin A, convertible to vitamin A in the body, commonly found in fruits and vegetables.
2102.benefits: Antioxidant properties, source of vitamin A, supports vision and immune function
2102.risks: Potential lung cancer risk with high-dose supplementation in smokers, skin discoloration with excessive intake

2104.name: Brewed Black Tea
2104.description: Brewed infusion of fermented tea leaves containing polyphenols, caffeine, and trace nutrients.
2104.benefits: Source of antioxidants (polyphenols), mild stimulant (caffeine), potential antimicrobial properties
2104.risks: Caffeine sensitivity, potential moderate irritant to sensitive skin, possible mild staining of teeth

2144.name: Modified Corn Starch
2144.description: Chemically or physically treated starch derived from corn used as a thickener, stabilizer, or emulsifier in food products.
2144.benefits: Improves texture, stabilizes emulsions, thickening agent
2144.risks: Possible allergenicity, processing residues, ultra-processed ingredient

2242.name: Vanilla Beans
2242.description: Natural pods from the vanilla orchid containing vanillin and other aromatic compounds used primarily for flavoring.
2242.benefits: Flavoring agent, natural aromatic compounds, culinary and fragrance uses
2242.risks: Possible mild skin irritation or sensitization in rare cases, minimal ingestion toxicity at typical culinary use

2262.name: Lycopene
2262.description: A red carotenoid pigment found in tomatoes and other red fruits, used as a food colorant and antioxidant.
2262.benefits: Antioxidant activity, may contribute to reduced oxidative damage

2274.name: Clarified Lemon Juice Concentrate
2274.description: Concentrated lemon juice with reduced pulp and particulates, primarily used as a flavoring and acidity regulator.
2274.benefits: Provides natural lemon flavor, acidity regulation in food products
2274.risks: Irritant to skin or mucous membranes in some individuals, potential for allergic reaction

2293.name: Magnesium Stearate
2293.description: A magnesium salt of stearic acid used as a lubricant and flow agent in pharmaceutical and supplement manufacturing.
2293.benefits: Improves powder flow, prevents ingredient clumping, aids manufacturing consistency
2293.risks: Potential minor irritation in sensitive individuals, possible interference with absorption at high doses

2315.name: Elderberry Extract
2315.description: Concentrated extract derived from Sambucus nigra berries, commonly used for flavoring, antioxidant properties, and topical application.
2315.benefits: Antioxidant properties, source of flavonoids, used for flavor and as a traditional botanical extract
2315.risks: Potential for allergic reactions, possible irritation in sensitive individuals, limited data on ingestion safety at high doses

2322.name: Mango
2322.description: Fruit composed primarily of carbohydrates, fiber, vitamins, and minerals. Commonly consumed fresh or processed.
2322.benefits: Source of dietary fiber, vitamin C, vitamin A precursors, antioxidants
2322.risks: Possible allergen for sensitive individuals, potential pesticide residue depending on cultivation, excessive intake may cause gastrointestinal discomfort

2331.name: Chaga Mushroom (Inonotus obliquus)
2331.description: Chaga mushroom is a parasitic fungus found mainly on birch trees, used traditionally in folk medicine. It contains polysaccharides, phenolic compounds, and antioxidants, and is being studied for its immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory properties.
2331.benefits: Antioxidant activity, anti-inflammatory effects, immune modulation, potential anticancer properties
2331.risks: Risk of oxalate kidney stones, may interact with anticoagulant medications, potential hypoglycemic effects, allergic reactions

2404.name: Black Cherry
2404.description: Black cherry is a fruit rich in vitamins, antioxidants, and anti-inflammatory compounds. It contains anthocyanins which may support cardiovascular health and reduce oxidative stress. Generally recognized as safe and nutritious when consumed as whole fruit or juice.
2404.benefits: Rich in antioxidants, anti-inflammatory, supports heart health, may reduce muscle soreness
2404.risks: Rare allergic reactions, potential interaction with blood-thinning medications

2522.name: Matcha
2522.description: Powdered green tea leaves primarily used for flavoring and antioxidant content.
2522.benefits: Antioxidant properties, contains polyphenols, enhances flavor
2522.risks: Caffeine content may cause mild stimulant effects, potential for allergic reactions

2561.name: Black Tea Leaves
2561.description: Processed leaves of Camellia sinensis, commonly used to prepare black tea. Contains polyphenols, caffeine, and flavor compounds.
2561.benefits: Contains antioxidants (polyphenols), supports hydration with stimulant effect, commonly consumed beverage
2561.risks: Caffeine-related sensitivity, potential pesticide residues depending on source

2564.name: Natural Raspberry Flavor
2564.description: Concentrated flavoring derived from raspberry fruit compounds, used to impart raspberry taste in food and beverages.
2564.benefits: Provides raspberry flavor without added sugars or calories, enhances palatability
2564.risks: Potential irritant or sensitizer in sensitive individuals, may contain trace solvents from extraction, lack of transparency in specific constituents

2577.name: Organic Blueberry Juice
2577.description: Juice derived from blueberries rich in anthocyanins and antioxidants.

2584.name: Organic Hibiscus
2584.description: Organic hibiscus refers to the dried petals of Hibiscus sabdariffa, cultivated without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. In food products, it provides a tart flavor and red color, and in the body, it is known for its antioxidant and potential antihypertensive properties.
2584.benefits: Rich in antioxidants, supports cardiovascular health, may lower blood pressure, anti-inflammatory properties
2584.risks: Possible drug interactions (with antihypertensive medications), mild gastrointestinal upset in sensitive individuals

2586.name: Guava Puree
2586.description: Purée made from guava fruit, used as a flavor and nutrient source in food products.
2586.benefits: Source of dietary fiber, vitamins (notably vitamin C), antioxidants

2600.name: Chamomile
2600.description: Herbal extract from dried flowers of the Matricaria recutita plant, commonly used for its calming properties and mild anti-inflammatory effects.
2600.benefits: Mild anti-inflammatory effects, soothing properties, used topically and in teas for calming effects
2600.risks: Allergic reactions and skin sensitization in sensitive individuals, possible cross-reactivity with related plants (e.g. ragweed), rare contact dermatitis

2620.name: Lemon Juice Powder
2620.description: Dehydrated powder form of lemon juice, primarily used for flavoring and as a source of organic acids and bioactive compounds such as vitamin C and flavonoids.
2620.benefits: Provides natural flavoring, source of vitamin C and antioxidants, shelf-stable compared to fresh lemon juice
2620.risks: Potential for mild irritation in high concentrations, sensitivity reactions in some individuals, possible residual pesticides if not properly processed

2626.name: Organic Inulin
2626.description: A soluble dietary fiber commonly extracted from chicory root, used as a prebiotic fiber to support gut health.
2626.benefits: Prebiotic fiber promoting beneficial gut microbiota, aids digestive health
2626.risks: Gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses including bloating, gas, and diarrhea

2633.name: Organic Ashwagandha Extract
2633.description: Extract from the root of Withania somnifera standardized to 0.5% withanolides, commonly used as a botanical supplement.
2633.benefits: Botanical source of withanolides, potential adaptogenic effects supporting stress response
2633.risks: Irritation or sensitization in sensitive individuals, potential interactions with medications, limited data on long-term safety

2636.name: Organic Nutmeg
2636.description: Nutmeg is a spice derived from the seed of Myristica fragrans, used primarily for flavoring in food.
2636.risks: Irritant and sensitizer at high doses, ingestion toxicity due to myristicin content which can cause hallucinations or poisoning in large amounts

2659.name: Cottonseed Oil
2659.description: Edible oil extracted from the seeds of the cotton plant, commonly used for cooking and food processing. It is high in polyunsaturated fatty acids.
2659.benefits: Provides a source of unsaturated fats, suitable for frying due to relatively high smoke point
2659.risks: High omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acid content, oxidation instability leading to rancidity, potential pesticide residue contamination, processing via hexane extraction

2694.name: Tangerine Juice
2694.description: Tangerine juice is a liquid extracted from tangerines, a citrus fruit rich in vitamin C, flavonoids, and various phytonutrients. It provides antioxidant activity and supports immune function in the body.
2694.benefits: High vitamin C content, antioxidant effects, potential support for immune health, source of potassium, contains phytonutrients
2694.risks: High in natural sugars, potential oral acidity, may interact with certain medications

2704.name: Carob Bean Gum
2704.description: Natural polysaccharide extracted from the seeds of the carob tree, used as a thickening and stabilizing agent in foods.
2704.benefits: Thickening, stabilizing, emulsifying properties, soluble dietary fiber
2704.risks: Potential mild gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals, rare allergenic potential

2711.name: Alpha-Tocopheryl Acetate
2711.description: A synthetic form of vitamin E used as an antioxidant in foods and cosmetics to protect oils and fats from oxidation.
2711.benefits: Antioxidant properties, helps prevent oxidative damage in formulations, supports vitamin E nutritional intake
2711.risks: Rare skin irritation or sensitization in topical use, low toxicity at typical intake levels

2713.name: Orange Juice from Concentrate
2713.description: Juice reconstituted from concentrated orange juice, providing flavor and nutritional components such as vitamin C and natural sugars.
2713.benefits: Source of vitamin C and antioxidants, hydration, natural flavoring
2713.risks: High sugar content leading to excessive calorie intake if consumed in large amounts, potential dental erosion risk from acidity

2714.name: Orange Pulp
2714.description: Fibrous material derived from the edible part of oranges, primarily composed of dietary fiber, water, and residual sugars.
2714.benefits: Dietary fiber source, supports digestive health, contains natural vitamins and antioxidants

2716.name: Strawberry Juice from Concentrate
2716.description: Juice derived from strawberries concentrated by removing water, then reconstituted for use in foods and beverages.
2716.benefits: Source of natural flavor and color, contains some vitamins and antioxidants from strawberries
2716.risks: Potential allergen for sensitive individuals, high natural sugar content, possible processing residues

2721.name: Pear Juice from Concentrate
2721.description: Pear juice from concentrate is made by extracting pear juice, removing most of its water to create a concentrate, then reconstituting it with water for use in foods and beverages. It provides natural fruit sugars and some vitamins, but processing removes most fiber and micronutrients.
2721.benefits: Provides hydration, contains some vitamin C and potassium
2721.risks: High in free sugars, low in fiber, possible spike in blood glucose, loss of polyphenols and micronutrients due to processing

2722.name: Passion Fruit Juice from Concentrate
2722.description: Juice derived from the concentration and reconstitution of passion fruit, commonly used as a flavoring and beverage ingredient.
2722.benefits: Source of vitamins and antioxidants, provides natural flavor and sweetness
2722.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, possible pesticide residues depending on agricultural practices, high natural sugar content

2723.name: Pineapple Juice from Concentrate
2723.description: Reconstituted juice made by adding water to pineapple juice concentrate, containing natural fruit sugars and organic acids.
2723.benefits: Source of vitamins (notably vitamin C), natural flavor and hydration
2723.risks: High sugar content, potential dental erosion from acidity

2725.name: Peach Purée
2725.description: A processed fruit ingredient made by mashing or blending ripe peaches into a thick, sauce-like consistency, primarily used for flavoring or as a sweetener in foods.
2725.benefits: Provides natural flavor and sweetness, source of dietary fiber and micronutrients such as vitamins A and C
2725.risks: Possible allergen for sensitive individuals, potential microbial contamination if improperly processed or stored

2742.name: Organic Strawberry Puree
2742.description: Pureed strawberries, usually used as a flavoring or ingredient in foods and beverages. Contains natural sugars, fiber, vitamins, and antioxidants.
2742.benefits: Source of dietary fiber, vitamin C, antioxidants
2742.risks: Possible allergen for strawberry-sensitive individuals, sugar content when consumed in excess

2748.name: Natural Grape Strawberry Flavor
2748.description: This ingredient refers to a blend of chemical extracts and concentrates derived from grape, strawberry, or similar natural sources, intended to mimic the taste of those fruits. It often contains solvents, carriers, and minor additives, and its use in foods is primarily for taste enhancement rather than nutrition.
2748.risks: Lack of transparency, may contain solvents or preservatives, ultra-processed, no nutritional value

2755.name: Magnesium hydroxide
2755.description: An inorganic compound used primarily as an antacid and laxative, also utilized in water treatment and as a flame retardant.
2755.benefits: Antacid properties, laxative effect, flame retardant, pH neutralizer
2755.risks: Mild gastrointestinal irritation at high doses, possible laxative effect, minimal dermal or inhalation toxicity

2778.name: Orange zest
2778.description: Orange zest is the outer colorful layer of the orange peel, rich in essential oils such as limonene and containing various phytonutrients and antioxidants. It is commonly used to add flavor, aroma, and small amounts of micronutrients to foods.
2778.benefits: Antioxidant properties, source of vitamin C, contains flavonoids, contributes dietary fiber, provides natural essential oils with anti-inflammatory effects
2778.risks: Allergic reactions (rare), pesticide residues (if not organic)

2802.name: Copper Sulfate
2802.description: Copper sulfate is an inorganic compound frequently used as a supplement in animal and plant nutrition, as well as an additive in some processed foods for its essential trace mineral copper content. In the human body, copper is necessary in small amounts for enzymatic reactions and iron metabolism.
2802.benefits: Provides copper, an essential trace mineral for enzymatic function, iron metabolism, and antioxidant defense
2802.risks: Potential toxicity at high doses, gastrointestinal irritation, liver and kidney damage with chronic exposure, not recommended for direct human supplementation without medical oversight

2808.name: Natural Mineral Water
2808.description: Water sourced from natural springs containing various dissolved minerals. Primarily used for hydration.
2808.benefits: Hydration, source of minerals such as calcium, magnesium, and bicarbonates
2808.risks: Potential contamination with heavy metals or microbiological agents depending on source quality

2855.name: Trace Minerals
2855.description: Minerals present in small amounts obtained from purified seawater, including elements such as magnesium, calcium, potassium, and others needed in trace quantities.
2855.benefits: Provides essential minerals for physiological functions at trace levels, supports electrolyte balance and metabolic processes
2855.risks: Contamination potential if purification is incomplete, intake of heavy metals if sourced improperly, irritation potential if used topically in high concentration

2873.name: Deionized Water
2873.description: Purified water from which ions and minerals have been removed. Used as a solvent and diluent in cleaning formulations.
2873.benefits: Non-toxic, non-irritating, solvent and carrier for other ingredients

2876.name: Calcium Hydroxide
2876.description: An inorganic compound used as a raising agent in foods to leaven or modify texture.
2876.benefits: Leavening agent, improves texture and processing in food products
2876.risks: Irritation risk if ingested in large quantities, high pH causing mucosal irritation

2913.name: Blueberry Puree
2913.description: Blueberry puree is made by mashing whole blueberries into a thick liquid or paste, retaining much of the fruit's natural nutrients and bioactive compounds.
2913.benefits: Source of dietary antioxidants, vitamins, and dietary fiber

2914.name: Blackberry Puree
2914.description: Pureed form of blackberry fruit containing water, fiber, natural sugars, vitamins, and antioxidants.
2914.benefits: Source of dietary fiber, vitamins, antioxidants
2914.risks: Minimal risk at typical use levels, potential for microbial contamination if not properly processed

2980.name: Carbonated Filtered Water
2980.description: Water that has been filtered for impurities and infused with carbon dioxide gas under pressure to create carbonation. Widely consumed and generally recognized as safe for consumption.
2980.benefits: Hydration, calorie-free beverage, alternative to sugary sodas

2982.name: Ginger Extract
2982.description: Ginger extract is a concentrated form of bioactive compounds from the ginger root (Zingiber officinale), commonly used for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties in both food products and supplements.
2982.benefits: Anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, may reduce nausea, may support digestion
2982.risks: Possible gastrointestinal discomfort, may interact with anticoagulant medications

3246.name: Monk Fruit Extract
3246.description: Sweetener derived from monk fruit (Siraitia grosvenorii) containing natural glycosides like mogrosides responsible for sweetness.
3246.benefits: Zero-calorie natural sweetener, does not raise blood glucose, alternative to sugar
3246.risks: Rare sensitization potential, lack of long-term safety data in large populations

3276.name: Natural Aroma
3276.description: A general term for flavoring substances derived from natural sources, often a complex mixture of volatile compounds. May contain trace allergens such as milk.
3276.risks: Allergen cross-contamination (milk), lack of transparency, potential sensitizer, ultra-processed

3282.name: Orange Peel
3282.description: Dried or processed rind of orange fruit used for flavoring and aroma.
3282.benefits: Provides natural citrus flavor, source of dietary fiber and antioxidant compounds
3282.risks: Potential for mild skin or mucous membrane irritation, pesticide residue contamination if not organic, ingestion generally safe in food amounts

3289.name: Organic Mango Purée
3289.description: Fruit purée made from organic mango, used as a flavoring and sweetening ingredient in food products.
3289.benefits: Source of vitamins (notably vitamin C), natural sugars, flavor enhancer

3327.name: Raspberry Juice Concentrate
3327.description: Fruit juice derived from raspberries, concentrated to remove water then reconstituted; primarily provides flavor and some nutritional components such as vitamins and antioxidants.
3327.benefits: Source of antioxidants, vitamins, natural flavor
3327.risks: Potential allergen for sensitive individuals, contains natural sugars

3328.name: Safflower Concentrate
3328.description: Concentrated extract or oil derived from safflower seeds, primarily a source of polyunsaturated fatty acids, notably linoleic acid (omega-6). Commonly used as an edible oil or ingredient in food products.
3328.benefits: Source of polyunsaturated fatty acids, contributes essential fatty acids
3328.risks: High omega-6 fatty acid content associated with oxidative instability, potential pro-inflammatory effects with excessive intake

3351.name: Lemon Concentrate
3351.description: Concentrated juice derived from lemons, containing primarily citric acid, vitamin C, and natural flavor compounds.
3351.benefits: Source of vitamin C, flavor enhancer, natural acidulant
3351.risks: Irritation to skin or mucous membranes in concentrated form, potential for acid damage to tooth enamel if ingested in large amounts

3367.name: Calcium D-Pantothenate
3367.description: Calcium D-pantothenate is the calcium salt of pantothenic acid (vitamin B5), used as a nutritional supplement and fortifier to support metabolic functions.
3367.benefits: Supports coenzyme A synthesis, aids energy metabolism, essential vitamin

3381.name: Lemon Extract
3381.description: Concentrated preparation derived from lemon fruit, containing flavor and aroma compounds primarily used for flavoring purposes.
3381.benefits: Provides natural citrus flavor and aroma
3381.risks: Irritation or sensitization risk for some individuals upon skin contact or ingestion in high amounts

3393.name: Niacinamide (Niacin)
3393.description: Niacinamide is a form of vitamin B3 (niacin), an essential water-soluble vitamin involved in numerous cellular processes including energy metabolism and DNA repair. It is commonly added to fortified foods and supplements to prevent vitamin B3 deficiency.
3393.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, helps maintain healthy skin and nervous system, prevents pellagra (niacin deficiency disease), supports DNA repair
3393.risks: Flushing at high doses, GI irritation at very high intakes, rare liver toxicity with prolonged large doses

3441.name: Organic Apple Juice Concentrate
3441.description: Concentrated juice derived from organic apples used primarily as a sweetener or flavor enhancer in food products.
3441.benefits: Natural source of sugars, provides flavor and sweetness
3441.risks: High sugar content, excessive intake associated with weight gain and dental caries

3510.name: Fumaric Acid
3510.description: An organic acid used as a food additive for acidity regulation and as a preservative.
3510.benefits: Acidity regulator, preservative, enhances shelf life
3510.risks: Irritation at high concentrations, potential sensitizer in rare cases

3511.name: Paprika Oleoresin
3511.description: A natural color additive derived from paprika peppers, containing carotenoids such as capsanthin and capsorubin used for coloring food and cosmetic products.
3511.benefits: Provides natural red-orange color, antioxidant carotenoids present
3511.risks: Irritation and sensitization potential in sensitive individuals, possible contamination with pesticide residues depending on source

3523.name: Organic Ginger Extract
3523.description: Organic ginger extract is a concentrated form of the bioactive compounds found in ginger (Zingiber officinale), commonly used for its flavor, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and digestive properties.
3523.benefits: Anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, supports digestive health, may reduce nausea, may aid in blood sugar regulation
3523.risks: Mild gastrointestinal discomfort, possible interaction with anticoagulant medications, potential allergic reactions

3536.name: Tapioca Dextrin
3536.description: A carbohydrate derived from tapioca starch, used as a thickener, stabilizer, or filler in food products.
3536.benefits: Provides texture and stability in foods, gluten-free carbohydrate source
3536.risks: Minor digestive intolerance in sensitive individuals, generally low concern

3541.name: Cold pressed Meyer lemon juice
3541.description: Cold pressed Meyer lemon juice is made by mechanically extracting juice from Meyer lemons without heat or solvents, preserving vitamin C, flavonoids, and aromatic compounds.
3541.benefits: High in vitamin C, provides flavonoids, antioxidant properties, may support immune function
3541.risks: Possible dental enamel erosion if consumed excessively, potential allergic reactions

3548.name: Peach juice (0.1%) from concentrate
3548.description: Peach juice from concentrate is made by extracting the water from peach juice to form a concentrate, which is then reconstituted with water before use; the low percentage indicates minimal peach-derived nutrients in the final product.
3548.risks: Ultra-processed, minimal phytonutrients, potential residual processing compounds

3828.name: Pyridoxine HCl (Vitamin B6)
3828.description: Water-soluble vitamin important for amino acid metabolism and neurological function. Often used in supplements as pyridoxine hydrochloride.
3828.benefits: Supports metabolism, neurotransmitter synthesis, immune function
3828.risks: Possible sensory neuropathy in high doses, rare allergic reactions

3965.name: Potassium Chloride (Electrolyte)
3965.description: Potassium chloride is a mineral salt commonly used as a dietary electrolyte and as a salt substitute to help maintain normal cellular function and fluid balance. In food products, it is often added to replace sodium or support electrolyte content.
3965.benefits: Essential for nerve and muscle function, helps maintain fluid and electrolyte balance, may help reduce high blood pressure as sodium substitute
3965.risks: Hyperkalemia in susceptible individuals, gastrointestinal irritation in large doses, contraindicated in kidney disease

3980.name: Natürliches Mineralwasser
3980.description: Natürliches Mineralwasser (natural mineral water) is water sourced from underground reservoirs, containing naturally occurring minerals and trace elements. It is bottled at the source and is typically free from chemical processing, making it a common beverage in many countries.
3980.benefits: Source of hydration, provides trace minerals, generally free from artificial additives
3980.risks: Potential for residual contaminants, possible heavy metal content, may lack essential electrolytes depending on mineral composition

4005.name: Filtered Carbonated Water
4005.description: Water purified through filtration and infused with carbon dioxide gas to create effervescence.
4005.risks: Mild acidity that may cause dental enamel erosion with excessive consumption

4012.name: Pristine Water
4012.description: Frozen pure water applied as a protective ice glaze on frozen seafood to prevent dehydration and oxidation during storage.
4012.benefits: Protects product quality by reducing dehydration and oxidation during frozen storage
4012.risks: None at typical use, potential for microbial contamination if water quality is poor

4024.name: Organic Lime Juice Concentrate
4024.description: Concentrated juice from limes, used primarily for flavoring and as an acidulant in foods and beverages.
4024.benefits: Provides vitamin C, natural flavoring, acidic preservative properties
4024.risks: Irritation to skin and mucous membranes in sensitive individuals, potential oral sensitivity with excessive consumption

4029.name: Organic Lime Flavor
4029.description: Organic lime flavor is a natural flavoring derived from organic limes or lime oils, used to impart a citrus taste to foods and beverages. Despite being labeled 'organic,' it is often processed, and exact composition is rarely disclosed to consumers.
4029.risks: Lack of transparency, potential for solvent residues, ultra-processed, no nutritional value

4114.name: Natural Green Tea Caffeine
4114.description: Caffeine is a stimulant found in green tea that acts on the central nervous system to increase alertness and reduce fatigue.
4114.benefits: Cognitive alertness, mild stimulant effects, possible antioxidant properties due to associated green tea compounds
4114.risks: Irritation/sensitization risk at high doses, potential for jitteriness, increased heart rate, sleep disturbances, possible interactions with certain medications

4115.name: Organic L-Theanine (from Green Tea)
4115.description: L-Theanine is an amino acid found primarily in green tea leaves. It is known for its calming effects, modulation of brain neurotransmitters, and ability to promote relaxation without drowsiness.
4115.benefits: May improve relaxation, may reduce stress, may enhance focus, may help with mild anxiety

4120.name: Organic Cranberry Juice Concentrate
4120.description: Concentrated cranberry juice reconstituted with water, used as a flavoring and source of natural phytochemicals.
4120.benefits: Source of antioxidants and phytochemicals, provides natural flavor and nutrients
4120.risks: High natural sugar content, potential digestive upset with excessive intake

4144.name: Organic Blueberry Flavor
4144.description: Flavoring derived from organic blueberries or their extracts, used to impart blueberry taste in foods. Typically considered a food ingredient; organic designation implies avoidance of synthetic pesticides.
4144.benefits: Provides natural blueberry aroma and taste, may contain trace antioxidants from blueberries

4289.name: Arginine Nitrate
4289.description: Inorganic compound commonly found in vegetables, water, and as a food additive; used as a preservative and color fixative in processed meats.
4289.benefits: Preserves food by inhibiting microbial growth, extends shelf life, and maintains color in cured meats
4289.risks: Potential formation of carcinogenic nitrosamines under acidic or high-heat conditions, contamination in drinking water leading to methemoglobinemia especially in infants

4357.name: Black Carrot Concentrate (Color)
4357.description: Natural colorants derived from grape and black carrot, rich in anthocyanin pigments used for food coloring.
4357.benefits: Natural coloring agent, antioxidant properties, derived from food sources
4357.risks: Potential allergic sensitization in sensitive individuals, possible contamination depending on extraction process

4375.name: Black Carrot Extract
4375.description: Extract derived from black carrots, primarily containing anthocyanins and other phenolic compounds used as natural colorants and antioxidants.
4375.risks: Low irritation potential, possible allergen in sensitive individuals, minimal contamination risk at typical use levels

4416.name: Purified Carbonated Water
4416.description: Purified carbonated water is water into which carbon dioxide gas under pressure has been dissolved. It's commonly used as a base in soft drinks and some other beverages. Purified means that the water has undergone processes to remove impurities, ensuring a higher level of cleanliness.
4416.risks: May leach minerals from the body, ultra-processed, associated with microplastic exposure

4452.name: Organic Gum Acacia
4452.description: Gum Acacia, also known as gum arabic, is a natural gum derived from the hardened sap of the Acacia tree. It is commonly used as an emulsifier, thickening agent, and stabilizer in food products. It's considered a prebiotic fiber, supporting gut health, and is Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS) by the FDA.
4452.benefits: Prebiotic fiber, supports gut microbiota, may improve satiety, well-tolerated in moderate amounts
4452.risks: Possible mild digestive discomfort at high intakes, rare allergic reactions

4567.name: Carbonated Spring Water
4567.description: Water sourced from a natural spring, infused with carbon dioxide gas for carbonation.
4567.benefits: Hydration, alternative to still water with sensory variation

4588.name: Natural Orange Flavor
4588.description: Flavoring derived from orange, used to impart citrus aroma and taste.
4588.risks: Possible mild irritation or sensitization in sensitive individuals, lack of transparency in composition

4611.name: Carbonated Coconut Water
4611.description: Coconut water is a clear liquid from young coconuts, naturally rich in electrolytes including potassium, magnesium, and sodium. Carbonation refers to the addition of dissolved carbon dioxide gas, giving it a fizzy texture but not significantly altering the base nutritional profile.
4611.benefits: Hydration, provides electrolytes (potassium, magnesium), low calorie
4611.risks: Potential digestive discomfort in sensitive individuals (from carbonation), rarely high potassium in kidney disease

4629.name: Organic Elderberry Juice from Concentrate
4629.description: Elderberry juice is derived from the fruit of the Sambucus nigra plant and is used for its antioxidant content and potential immune-supporting properties. When labeled 'from concentrate,' water is removed and then added back, often involving heat processing.
4629.benefits: Rich in anthocyanins, antioxidant activity, may support immune function
4629.risks: Possible allergic reactions, mild gastrointestinal discomfort

4645.name: Organic Raw Honey
4645.description: Natural sweetener produced by bees from nectar, minimally processed to retain enzymes and bioactive compounds.
4645.benefits: Natural sweetener, contains trace antioxidants and enzymes, minimal processing preserves some bioactive compounds
4645.risks: Potential for botulism in infants under 1 year, high sugar content leading to dental caries and elevated calorie intake

4667.name: Sour Cherry Juice Concentrate
4667.description: Sour cherry juice concentrate is a reduced, highly concentrated form of sour cherry juice, commonly used as a flavoring, sweetener, or coloring in foods and beverages. It retains many of the bioactive compounds found in whole sour cherries, including polyphenols and anthocyanins, which have antioxidant properties.
4667.benefits: Antioxidant properties, anti-inflammatory effects, may improve recovery after exercise, may benefit sleep quality
4667.risks: High natural sugar content, possible dental caries risk if consumed in excess

4988.name: Carrot Powder
4988.description: Powdered form of dried carrots, used primarily as a natural colorant and flavoring agent with nutritional content including beta-carotene.
4988.benefits: Source of beta-carotene and antioxidants, natural colorant, provides some nutrients
4988.risks: Low irritation potential, possible allergen for sensitive individuals

5018.name: Organic Lion's Mane Extract
5018.description: Lion's mane (Hericium erinaceus) is a medicinal mushroom used in traditional medicine, known for its potential neuroprotective properties. Lion's mane extract is derived from the fruiting body or mycelium and is commonly marketed as a nootropic or cognitive-support supplement. The 'organic' label indicates it is grown without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. Classified as GRAS (Generally Recognized As Safe) in supplemental use, but long-term safety data are limited.
5018.benefits: Neuroprotective effects, potential cognitive enhancement, anti-inflammatory properties, antioxidant activity
5018.risks: Rare allergic reactions, insufficient long-term safety data

5052.name: Retinyl Palmitate
5052.description: A synthetic ester of retinol (vitamin A) used in skincare for its provitamin A activity and skin renewal properties.
5052.benefits: Supports skin cell turnover and collagen production
5052.risks: Skin irritation, photosensitivity, potential teratogenicity at high systemic exposure, instability to light and air

5054.name: Cholecalciferol
5054.description: Cholecalciferol is Vitamin D3, a fat-soluble vitamin important for calcium homeostasis and bone metabolism.
5054.benefits: Supports bone health, calcium absorption, immune function
5054.risks: Hypercalcemia with excessive intake, potential toxicity at high doses

5074.name: Magnesium L-Threonate
5074.description: Magnesium L-Threonate is a chelated form of magnesium bound to L-threonic acid. It is designed for better absorption and central nervous system bioavailability compared to other magnesium salts. Often used as a dietary supplement to support cognitive function and brain health. Recognized as safe by regulatory agencies when used appropriately.
5074.benefits: Improved brain magnesium levels, potential cognitive enhancement, supports memory and learning, neuroprotective effects
